summary: A [presidential committee](2025-05-28-presidential-committee-dpi-implementation) and a [civil service working committee](2026-08-17-nigeria-hos-digital-transformation-working-committee) sit above a [digital public infrastructure framework](2025-03-07-dpi-framework-unified-services-2027) still in development against a 2027 services target.
developments:
The presidential committee on implementation was constituted in May 2025 and is operating ([committee](2025-05-28-presidential-committee-dpi-implementation)).

An eleven-member civil service technical working committee was inaugurated in August 2026, tasked with drafting the architecture, roadmap and governance mechanisms within one week ahead of a steering committee; no terms of reference, budget or publication commitment is stated ([working committee](2026-08-17-nigeria-hos-digital-transformation-working-committee)).

The framework itself remains in development against a target of 75 per cent of public services digitised by 2027 on an integrated-government model ([framework](2025-03-07-dpi-framework-unified-services-2027)).

summary: The [National Telecommunications Policy](2026-05-22 Why global hyperscalers are avoiding Nigeria despite Africa's biggest market) is being rewritten for the first time since 2000, a licensing regime built for voice and messaging.
developments:
The rewrite was under way in May 2026 ([rewrite](2026-05-22 Why global hyperscalers are avoiding Nigeria despite Africa's biggest market)).

A licensing regime built for voice and short messaging is cited as a reason hyperscalers route investment to other African markets, which is the argument the rewrite has to answer. No draft, timetable or consultation is published.

summary: A [Spectrum Roadmap 2026-2030](2026-03-01-ncc-spectrum-roadmap-2026-2030) would raise assignable spectrum from 1.07 GHz to about 3.8 GHz, and [about 3,700 towers](2026-08-19-guardianng-fg-3700-towers-nucap-20m-nigerians) are to deploy from October 2026.
developments:
The roadmap targets at least 96 per cent 4G population coverage and at least 50 per cent for 5G by 2030, sets a median quality benchmark rising from 20-22 Mbps to 65-80 Mbps, and treats satellite direct-to-device as the complement for riverine, border and blackspot communities ([roadmap](2026-03-01-ncc-spectrum-roadmap-2026-2030)); the universal service fund identifies 87 clusters holding approximately 23 million people ([roadmap](2026-03-01-ncc-spectrum-roadmap-2026-2030)).

Resource mobilisation and contracting are stated complete for about 3,700 towers reaching more than 20 million people, with a first tower in Delta State and riverine communities targeted before mid-2027 ([towers](2026-08-19-guardianng-fg-3700-towers-nucap-20m-nigerians)); the count, the population figure and the dates are the government's own and no contract value or supplier is stated ([towers](2026-08-19-guardianng-fg-3700-towers-nucap-20m-nigerians), [approval](2026-08-07-nigeria-project-bridge-fibre-rollout-approval)).

summary: A [National Digital Cloud Policy](2026-08-18-nigeria-national-digital-cloud-policy) makes cloud the default for new federal systems and sorts data into four levels, above [cloud guidelines signed with no published text](2026-08-04-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-regulatory-frameworks-signed) and a [draft data and cloud policy](2026-06-17 Government data silos threaten Nigeria's AI ambitions) five years in draft.
developments:
The policy is in force apart from its sovereignty provisions, which await presidential approval. It pools ministry demand through the government infrastructure company under framework agreements, and sorts government and regulated data into four levels, the highest hosted only in Nigeria and the next stored at rest in Nigeria; it imposes no general localisation on commercial data, and sets a private cloud and data-centre investment target of US$250m within 12 months rising to US$750m within 24 months ([policy](2026-08-18-nigeria-national-digital-cloud-policy), [announcement](2026-08-17-nigeria-national-digital-cloud-policy-fmcide-announcement)).

Cloud computing and technical guidelines were signed at a ceremony in August 2026 with implementation beginning immediately in phases, and scope, obligations and thresholds unstated because no text is published ([guidelines](2026-08-04-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-regulatory-frameworks-signed), [signing](2026-08-05-nitda-signs-sovereign-cloud-framework-to-boost-ai-data-centre-investment)).

A separate draft national policy on data and cloud has been in draft since 2021, and the localisation question was settled by circular instead ([draft](2026-06-17 Government data silos threaten Nigeria's AI ambitions)).

summary: [Draft technical standards for digital public infrastructure](2025-04-15-nitda-draft-dpi-technical-standards) have been in draft since April 2025 with nothing published since.
developments:
The standards were in draft in April 2025 and remain so ([standards](2025-04-15-nitda-draft-dpi-technical-standards)).

A national data exchange is meanwhile moving personal data in production behind the government service portal, so the exchange is running ahead of the standards that would govern it.

summary: The [National AI Strategy](2025-02-05-ai-connectivity-government-initiatives) is still in development with its Trust approved, while the country ranks [38th of 135 on a responsible-AI index](2026-08-10-nigeria-tops-africa-girai-responsible-ai-index) and Africa's highest.
developments:
The National AI Trust was approved by the Federal Executive Council in February 2025 to mobilise resources and provide oversight, building on a 2024 draft strategy and the national artificial-intelligence research centre; the strategy itself is still in development ([trust](2025-02-05-ai-connectivity-government-initiatives)).

The country scores 45.93 and 38th of 135 on the 2026 responsible-AI index, Africa's highest, and 72nd on a government readiness index against 141st three years earlier; the responsible-AI index's own conclusion is that holding policies is not the same as enforceable oversight or deployed systems, and both are composite scores built largely from policy documents ([indices](2026-08-10-nigeria-tops-africa-girai-responsible-ai-index)).

summary: A [central bank circular](2026-06-24-complyan-cbn-data-localisation-directive) requires payment data generated in Nigeria to be stored there by 1 January 2027, against [more than 85 per cent of workloads on public clouds](2026-08-11-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-google-microsoft-amazon).
developments:
The circular requires payment transaction data generated in Nigeria to be stored and managed in Nigeria by 1 January 2027, with ultimate beneficial ownership disclosure and market-concentration caps; the circular text itself is not held ([circular](2026-06-24-complyan-cbn-data-localisation-directive), [directive](2026-06-17-cbn-data-localisation-beneficial-owners-2027), [dilemma](2026-07-10 CBN's Data Localisation Directive Puts Nigerian Fintechs In A Cloud Dilemma)).

An analysing firm estimates US$850m a year spent on offshore data hosting and about 90 per cent of Nigerian payment data currently held abroad ([analysis](2026-08-12-nigeria-cbn-payments-system-circular-data-localisation)).

More than 85 per cent of Nigerian workloads sit on public clouds and 22 per cent of the thousand most-accessed sites are hosted locally against a 34 per cent sub-Saharan average ([dependence](2026-08-11-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-google-microsoft-amazon)); the concentration risk is an expert's characterisation rather than a measured exposure ([dependence](2026-08-11-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-google-microsoft-amazon), [costs](2026-08-26-cloud-dependence-african-ai-startups-cost-risks)).

summary: The [Data Protection Act 2023](2026-08-20-thesun-nigeria-fg-ngf-data-protection-act-states) is in force with an [amendment bill](2026-07-19-rulaac-nigeria-data-protection-amendment-bill-social-media) before the assembly, and the [first damages award](2026-08-01-fct-court-stanbic-ibtc-data-privacy-judgment) under it was made in July 2026.
developments:
The Act is criticised as structurally weak in placing the commission under ministerial control, and its section 63 gives it primacy over any inconsistent law on personal-data processing; the federal government and the governors' forum have been urging states to implement it, which is an admission that the tier handling civil registration, health, education and land records is not yet compliant ([Act](2026-08-20-thesun-nigeria-fg-ngf-data-protection-act-states), [accountability](2026-02-27 Who Protects Nigeria's Digital Citizens Unmasking Accountability Gaps in Digital Rights Governance)).

An amendment bill was introduced in July 2026 ([bill](2026-07-19-rulaac-nigeria-data-protection-amendment-bill-social-media)).

A court awarded ₦15m general damages, costs and post-judgment interest for marketing after consent was withdrawn, grounded on the Act, the constitutional privacy provision and the consumer-protection Act together; it held personal data must be erased on termination but refused wholesale deletion where statutory banking retention applies ([judgment](2026-08-01-fct-court-stanbic-ibtc-data-privacy-judgment)).

summary: The [Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act 2024](2025-08-01-cybercrime-act-misuse-n1-1trn) is in force, and lawyers argue enforcement agencies misapply it against dissent rather than cyber threats.
developments:
Civil-society lawyers argue the Act is misapplied against dissent, with most such cases collapsing because complainants never testify; the financial sector alone lost ₦53.4bn to cybercrime in 2024 ([Act](2025-08-01-cybercrime-act-misuse-n1-1trn)).

No prosecution, conviction or dismissal series under the Act is published, so the claim of misuse and the claim of necessity rest on the same absence of data.

summary: The [NIMC Act 2026](2026-08-02-nimc-act-2026-experts-transparency-data-protection) makes the identity number the foundational credential, and a [legal reading](2026-08-11-nigeria-nimc-act-2026-legal-analysis) puts mandatory use across passports, banking, telecommunications and land dealings.
developments:
The Act replaces the 2007 statute, recognises the identity number as the foundational credential under a one-person-one-identity policy, incorporates the data-protection regime and lets the commission prosecute identity fraud; the gazetted text was still not publicly available about six weeks after assent, so neither the expansion reading nor the counter-reading can be checked against it ([Act](2026-08-02-nimc-act-2026-experts-transparency-data-protection), [transformation](2026-07-22-thisday-shettima-digital-transformation-nimc-act-2026), [analysis](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act)).

On a law firm's reading the commission becomes the root certification authority for a national public key infrastructure and the national biometric-data repository, use of the number is made mandatory across four named sectors, the Act states that proof of identity is not proof of eligibility or citizenship, and unauthorised database access carries penalties of at least NGN10m or five years for an individual ([reading](2026-08-11-nigeria-nimc-act-2026-legal-analysis)).

summary: Crypto sits [inside the securities perimeter](2025-05-09-isa-2025-crypto-securities), an [executive order](2026-07-20-nigeria-coordinated-regulatory-framework-virtual-assets) created a coordinating council, [draft virtual-asset rules](2026-08-24-nigeria-sec-crypto-rules-itweb) set capital thresholds and a [stablecoin licensing regime](2026-06-17-cbn-nigeria-payments-system-vision-2028) is drafted.
developments:
The Investments and Securities Act 2025 put crypto inside the securities perimeter ([Act](2025-05-09-isa-2025-crypto-securities)), and an executive order of July 2026 created a Virtual Asset Council and Office with its secretariat at the central bank, creating no new regulator and transferring no powers ([order](2026-07-20-nigeria-coordinated-regulatory-framework-virtual-assets)).

Draft rules out for comment set N500m minimum capital for digital-asset platforms, N200m for service providers, a N30m registration fee, local incorporation and a resident chief executive ([rules](2026-08-24-nigeria-sec-crypto-rules-itweb), [data](2026-08-20-nigeria-sec-crypto-firms-share-transaction-data)).

A drafted issuer-licensing regime for fiat-collateralised stablecoins requires full reserves with licensed Nigerian banks, daily reconciliation and monthly audited publication; no instrument is issued ([regime](2026-06-17-cbn-nigeria-payments-system-vision-2028)). The securities regulator has admitted further firms to an incubation programme with no graduation route published ([incubation](2026-08-17-nigeria-sec-crypto-incubator-three-companies)), and the central bank intends to run observer nodes on approved stablecoin blockchains ([nodes](2026-08-21-nigeria-cbn-monitor-stablecoin-transactions)).

2026-08-31 — the same draft [also carries custody and incident duties: customer assets segregated from the firm's own with 80% held offline, N2bn minimum capital for exchanges and custodians, a fidelity bond of at least 25% of that minimum, incidents notified within 24 hours and reported within 48, and SEC approval before a foreign-issued stablecoin is listed](2026-08-31-techcabal-sec-crypto-custody). No commencement date or transition period is stated.

summary: A [risk-based regime](2026-01-14-nigeria-plans-ai-regulations-bill) sits in an unpassed bill, competition law was [turned on AI training over Nigerian journalism](2026-07-06-fccpc-directed-to-investigate-big-techs), and [judicial officers](2026-08-17-vanguard-digicivic-judicial-officers-digital-rights) called for authentication standards.
developments:
High-risk systems in finance, public administration, surveillance and automated decision-making would face annual impact assessments with fines up to ₦10m or 2 per cent of Nigerian revenue ([bill](2026-01-14-nigeria-plans-ai-regulations-bill)); an external reading finds the bill envisages risk assessment without categorising risk into levels, and a domestic critique warns it concentrates broad powers in agencies that lack proven capacity ([bill](2026-01-14-nigeria-plans-ai-regulations-bill), [control](2025-11-20-nigeria-ai-bill-control-innovation), [governance](2026-01-23-okolo-raji-global-majority-international-ai-governance)).

A presidential directive of July 2026 covers alleged anti-competitive practices, unlawful exploitation of news content and other unfair conduct by major global technology and generative artificial-intelligence firms; it followed a press-organisation petition and no terms of reference or interim finding is published ([directive](2026-07-06-fccpc-directed-to-investigate-big-techs), [scope](2026-08-24-fccpc-investigation-global-digital-platforms-analysis)).

Fifty-four judicial officers called for stricter authentication standards for AI-generated evidence and a review of the digital-evidence, cybercrime and privacy statutes; a communique carries no legal force and no legislative response is on record ([communique](2026-08-17-vanguard-digicivic-judicial-officers-digital-rights)). A university-system artificial-intelligence framework has been written and three tertiary regulators committed to harmonise ([tertiary](2026-08-02-nigeria-naaip-ai-guardrails-tertiary-institutions)).

progress: Mixed, a US$222m platform penalty under appeal and a local-presence bill in consultation while enforcement of new platform rules was paused
summary: A [US$222m consumer-protection penalty](2026-07-10 Nigeria tests data sovereignty as foreign tech firms facing probe) is under appeal, [enforcement of new platform rules was paused](2026-07-08 FG Halts Enforcement of New Regulations on Internet Platforms) in July 2026, and a [local-presence bill](2026-08-04-nigeria-sb648-plateformes-bureaux-locaux-dba) went to public consultation.
developments:
The penalty was imposed in 2025 and is under appeal, distinct from the data-protection track ([penalty](2026-07-10 Nigeria tests data sovereignty as foreign tech firms facing probe)).

The minister paused enforcement of new internet-platform rules pending a unified national digital-economy policy framework, convening a joint technical committee of three regulators to resolve overlapping mandates ([pause](2026-07-08 FG Halts Enforcement of New Regulations on Internet Platforms)).

An amendment requiring large platforms to maintain physical offices went to a Senate committee hearing and then to public consultation; a coalition backed passage on an investment case while a rights organisation calls for withdrawal over a power it reads as letting the commission prohibit a non-compliant platform's activities after thirty days without adequate judicial safeguards, and thresholds, deadlines, sanctions and appeal routes are still undefined ([bill](2026-08-04-nigeria-sb648-plateformes-bureaux-locaux-dba), [hearing](2026-07-29-project-sprint-senate-support-data-protection-bill), [legislation](2025-03-19-senate-social-media-legislation)).

summary: A [National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill](2025-11-11-digital-economy-egovernance-bill-nitda) before the assembly would elevate the technology agency to a super regulator, with overlap flagged by stakeholders.
developments:
The bill offers a unified legal framework with broad supervisory and enforcement powers, and also carries the risk-based artificial-intelligence regime ([bill](2025-11-11-digital-economy-egovernance-bill-nitda)).

Its electronic-signature provisions overlap with the root certification authority the identity statute already created, and which instrument governs digital signatures is unresolved on the record.

summary: The commission has taken [compliance above 55 per cent](2025-08-25-ndpc-probes-1369-organisations) on a remediation-first model, imposed a [₦766m penalty](2025-07-06-ndpc-multichoice-fine-statement), opened [multinational investigations](2025-03-24-ndpc-probes-tiktok-truecaller) and had a [platform fund its capacity programme](2026-06-09 Meta backs NDPC in landmark privacy initiative).
developments:
Compliance lifted from about 4 per cent of organisations to above 55 per cent by March 2025 ([enforcement](2025-08-25-ndpc-probes-1369-organisations)); twenty-one-day notices went to 1,369 organisations in 2025 and more than a thousand educational institutions in 2026, and a forensic investigation was opened in August 2026 into a federal university, a bank and a technology vendor over students' data allegedly used to open bank accounts without consent ([enforcement](2025-08-25-ndpc-probes-1369-organisations), [schools](2026-02-23-ndpc-probes-schools-data-privacy), [investigation](2026-08-13-nigeria-ndpc-investigates-unilag-lotus-bank)). The Federal High Court upheld the power to designate and register controllers of major importance, reaching agents, banks, telcos, health and digital platforms ([court](2026-07-28-federal-high-court-affirms-ndpc-authority-to-register-dcpmis)).

The largest fine to date, ₦766,242,500, was imposed expressly for want of cooperation, and whether it was paid, contested or varied is not established ([fine](2025-07-06-ndpc-multichoice-fine-statement)).

Multinational platforms are under investigation ([probes](2025-03-24-ndpc-probes-tiktok-truecaller)), and a two-year capacity programme is funded under a court-approved settlement with a United States platform ([settlement](2026-06-09 Meta backs NDPC in landmark privacy initiative)).

progress: Mixed, the Act's enforcement apparatus pointed at the public sector for the first time while the instrument doing it is not published
summary: A [circular directs every federal agency](2026-08-07-fij-ndpc-circular-mdas-not-published) to appoint data protection officers, and its own text is not in the public record; a [suit was filed against the electoral commission](2026-07-10 FIJ Showed That INEC Broke Data Law. Digital Rights Lawyers Sue the Commission 10 Months Later) for operating without a privacy policy.
developments:
The circular directs all ministries, departments and agencies to appoint qualified officers and register them, engage licensed compliance organisations, make budgetary provision and file audit returns, and makes permanent secretaries and chief executives personally responsible; it is the first instrument on file pointing the Act's enforcement apparatus at the public sector rather than at banks, schools and telcos, and searches of the government's own resource portal returned nothing three days after the announcement ([circular](2026-08-07-fij-ndpc-circular-mdas-not-published)).

A Federal High Court suit was filed against the electoral commission for operating without a website privacy policy, following an exposé and a voter-record leak ([suit](2026-07-10 FIJ Showed That INEC Broke Data Law. Digital Rights Lawyers Sue the Commission 10 Months Later)).

The commission has a memorandum with the communications regulator ([memorandum](2026-02-06-ncc-ndpc-data-protection-mou)) and agreed collaboration with the securities regulator with no joint supervisory arrangement stated ([collaboration](2026-08-14-nigeria-ndpc-sec-data-protection-collaboration)), while artificial-intelligence-generated identity fraud rose 192 per cent in one quarter as document forgery fell 80 ([fraud](2025-06-25-synthetic-id-fraud-sumsub-q1)).

summary: A [bilateral health memorandum](2025-12-19-afghs-mou-nigeria) and its [specimen sharing agreement](2025-12-19-afghs-specimen-sharing-agreement-nigeria) require sharing within five days of a United States request, against [membership of a cross-border privacy forum](2025-04-30-nigeria-joins-global-cbpr-privacy-forum).
developments:
The memorandum was signed in December 2025 with planned United States support of US$1,953,530,560 against Nigeria's US$2,975,634,499 ([memorandum](2025-12-19-afghs-mou-nigeria)); a rights organisation's reading of seven signed memoranda puts Nigeria among five whose text requires unilateral sharing of specimens and pathogen-sequencing data and among two whose data-sharing arrangement is deferred to an unpublished appendix, with all seven requiring broad audit access ([memorandum](2025-12-19-afghs-mou-nigeria), [assessment](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements), [complaint](2026-04-02-public-citizen-v-department-of-state-foia-complaint)). Every page is stamped not for public release.

The specimen agreement entered force in January 2026 for a renewable five-year term, requiring sharing within five days of a request with no numerical cap on onward sharing with non-governmental United States entities ([agreement](2025-12-19-afghs-specimen-sharing-agreement-nigeria)).

The country joined a global cross-border privacy rules forum in April 2025 ([forum](2025-04-30-nigeria-joins-global-cbpr-privacy-forum)).

summary: An [Abuja Declaration on meaningful connectivity](2026-07-29-meaningful-connectivity-africa-atu-pushes-digital-inclusion) was adopted with machinery to argue it internationally, and the country leads a [digital trade regulators group](2026-08-05-afcfta-digital-trade-forum-lagos-oduwole-mene) and a [trilateral customs committee](2026-07-31-benin-cameroon-nigeria-customs-border-modernisation-digital-interoperability).
developments:
The declaration was adopted at a continental conference in Abuja in July 2026, with machinery to argue the position at the international union ([declaration](2026-07-29-meaningful-connectivity-africa-atu-pushes-digital-inclusion)).

The country was named lead of a group harmonising market entry, licensing and regulatory cooperation for African digital service firms, with guidelines named as a first output and none published ([group](2026-08-05-afcfta-digital-trade-forum-lagos-oduwole-mene)).

A joint communique with two neighbours committed three customs administrations to a trilateral steering committee on digital interoperability, harmonised procedures and coordinated risk management at two corridors, with no funding, timeline or output published ([customs](2026-07-31-benin-cameroon-nigeria-customs-border-modernisation-digital-interoperability)), and an artificial-intelligence and cyber diplomacy unit sits inside the foreign ministry coordinating engagement on emerging technologies ([unit](2026-08-04-nigeria-now-west-africas-digital-powerhouse-says-tijani)).

progress: Mixed, a regional biometric card in issue while the continental cyber and data convention is unsigned
summary: The [regional biometric identity card](2025-11-28 Nigeria Unveils ECOWAS ID Card To Boost Regional Travel, Security) has been in issue since November 2025, while a peer-reviewed review records the country as a [non-signatory to the continental convention](2026-08-14-ssa-health-data-governance-literature-review).
developments:
The regional card entered issue in November 2025 to support regional travel and security ([card](2025-11-28 Nigeria Unveils ECOWAS ID Card To Boost Regional Travel, Security)).

A peer-reviewed review of health-data governance in four countries records only one of them as a signatory to the continental cyber and data convention, and finds all four frameworks fragmented with weak cross-border transfer harmonisation and capacity gaps ([review](2026-08-14-ssa-health-data-governance-literature-review)). A country issuing a regional credential while outside the regional data instrument is the shape here.

summary: The country is one of three first pilots for [shared cross-border identity, payment and data rails](2026-05-26-nigeria-kenya-morocco-afcfta-adapt), and a [subsea cable to Equatorial Guinea](2026-02-12-nigeria-equatorial-guinea-subsea-fibre) bundles a data centre with it.
developments:
The country implementation forum for the cross-border rails pilot was inaugurated in Abuja in July 2026 ([pilot](2026-07-30-nigeria-inaugurates-adapt-forum-digital-trade-afcfta), [selection](2026-05-26-nigeria-kenya-morocco-afcfta-adapt)).

The cable agreement was signed in February 2026 and bundles a commercial data centre, so local hosting rides in on the cross-border link ([cable](2026-02-12-nigeria-equatorial-guinea-subsea-fibre), [account](2026-02-24 Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea subsea cable strengthens connectivity)).

summary: A [government enterprise architecture](2026-04-07 NITDA Assumes Control Of NGEA Infrastructure) was handed to the technology agency in April 2026 and piloted at four agencies, alongside a [digital trustmark](2025-10-10-nitda-digital-trustmark-initiative).
developments:
The architecture was built over about two and a half years with a foreign development agency, is hosted by the government infrastructure company and was piloted at the identity commission, customs, immigration and the technology agency ([handover](2026-04-07 NITDA Assumes Control Of NGEA Infrastructure), [takeover](2026-03-27-nitda-takes-over-ngea-koica)).

A digital trustmark has been in issue since October 2025 ([trustmark](2025-10-10-nitda-digital-trustmark-initiative)). Neither carries a published conformance standard, adoption count or list of bound systems.

summary: Payments [migrated to ISO 20022](2025-08-27-cbn-pos-geotag-iso20022), crypto trades are [reported to the international framework](2026-01-12-tin-nin-crypto-tax-carf), the passport [joined the aviation key directory](2026-07-16-nigeria-icao-pkd-biometric-passport), and a [software assurance framework](2026-07-30-prnigeria-nitda-software-quality-assurance-framework) is proposed.
developments:
The payments migration completed in 2025 with point-of-sale geo-tagging ([migration](2025-08-27-cbn-pos-geotag-iso20022)), and crypto trade reporting against tax and identity numbers went live in January 2026 aligned to the international crypto-asset reporting framework ([reporting](2026-01-12-tin-nin-crypto-tax-carf)).

Integration with the civil aviation public key directory moved the passport from machine-readable to cryptographically verifiable at 111 member states' borders ([passport](2026-07-16-nigeria-icao-pkd-biometric-passport)).

A national software quality assurance framework consolidates development, testing and licensing guidelines with an accessibility standard for citizen-facing platforms, tiers risk with core banking and national identity infrastructure in the top class, makes certification a condition of project clearance and sets full operation for 2027; it is not adopted and no licensed testing organisation is on file ([framework](2026-07-30-prnigeria-nitda-software-quality-assurance-framework)); automated anti-money-laundering baseline standards were mandated in March 2026, shifting the test from tooling to governance, integration and explainability ([baseline](2026-03-12-cbn-automated-aml-baseline-standards)).

progress: Mixed, three frameworks advanced while the web design standards stalled with no toolkit published
summary: A [digital infrastructure assurance framework](2026-08-04-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-regulatory-frameworks-signed) was signed with no published text, an [innovation hub standards framework](2026-08-21-von-nigeria-innovation-hub-standards-framework) is at validation, and the [web design standards](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility) have published no toolkit a year on.
developments:
The assurance framework was signed in August 2026 with no published text and no stated obligations, thresholds or commencement date; the central bank tied the programme to financial stability on the ground that payment platforms, cloud, cybersecurity, networks and digital identity are now financial infrastructure ([assurance](2026-08-04-nigeria-sovereign-cloud-regulatory-frameworks-signed)).

A draft hub standards framework gives innovation hubs a self-assessment tool across seven dimensions and about thirty-five criteria, validated against a count of more than 339 hubs concentrated in two cities ([hubs](2026-08-21-von-nigeria-innovation-hub-standards-framework)).

The compensation framework binds mobile operators and fires where the commission confirms a missed quality target in a named local government area, paying automatic airtime credit with no appeal on the amount; the directive instrument itself is not published and the qualifying thresholds are referred out to regulations the base does not hold ([compensation](2026-08-05-ncc-framework-compensation-consumers)).

2026-08-31 — the web design standards, [launched in July 2025 with a toolkit promised within eight to ten weeks ahead of rule-making and Federal Executive Council approval, had published none by August 2026, and two publications searching public materials found no evidence of approval or implementation](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility). [The ministry's 2025 year in review still lists the launch as an achievement](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility). No revised timetable is published: the commitment stands unmet.

summary: A rights organisation and the editors' guild [jointly called for enforcement of the Cybercrimes Act to be suspended](2026-08-24-serap-nge-cybercrimes-act-suspension) pending repeal or revision, and no government response is on file.
developments:
The state security service offered to pause its cybercrimes prosecution of a campaigner until after the 2027 election, and was told that pausing is not the remedy sought ([report](2026-08-31-punchng-sowore-serap-dss-withdraw-charges)). The charges stand.

They argue the 2024 amendment failed to cure the defect a regional court identified in 2022 when it ruled the original cyberstalking section vague, arbitrary and in breach of the African Charter, and that the amended text keeps ambiguous wording under which a prosecution can turn on someone claiming to feel fear ([call](2026-08-24-serap-nge-cybercrimes-act-suspension)).

The call cites extrajudicial arrests, malicious prosecutions, enforced disappearances and unlawful surveillance reaching as far as posts in private messaging groups. No government or prosecutorial response is on file.

summary: A civil-society body built an [artificial-intelligence tracker of online gender-based violence](2026-08-01-nigeria-ai-enabled-ogbv-tracker) with more than 20,000 verified cases, and another [monitors parties digital-rights compliance](2026-08-08-nigeria-citad-pawsom-monitor-digital-rights-elections) at elections.
developments:
The tracker uses machine learning, localised keywords and context analysis to detect, categorise and monitor abuse in real time, flags actionable cases and produces evidence for referral; it is a civil-society body building the measurement layer the state has not ([tracker](2026-08-01-nigeria-ai-enabled-ogbv-tracker)).

A separate platform tracks political parties' websites and social media for data-privacy violations and access restrictions during elections, piloted at a state governorship election with no findings published ([monitor](2026-08-08-nigeria-citad-pawsom-monitor-digital-rights-elections)).

summary: A [50 per cent tariff reset](2025-01-20-ncc-approves-50-percent-tariff-increase) in 2025 and [removal of the 5 per cent telecom excise](2025-08-25-nigeria-abolishes-5pct-telecom-tax) preceded [about ₦2.13tn of sector capital spending](2026-08-06-telcos-call-for-policy-consistency-regulatory-certainty-nigeria) in 2025.
developments:
The tariff increase was the first in about eleven years, approved after naira devaluation drove sector losses reported at about US$11.3bn forgone over the freeze ([reset](2025-01-20-ncc-approves-50-percent-tariff-increase), [losses](2025-01-29-telcos-lost-11-billion-tariff-delay)), and the excise duty was removed in August 2025 ([excise](2025-08-25-nigeria-abolishes-5pct-telecom-tax)).

The operators' association puts about ₦2.13tn invested in 2025 with about ₦1.86tn planned for 2026, credits the tariff adjustment with moving the industry from severe financial pressure to reinvestment, and says a substantial share is financed from domestic capital that capital-importation statistics never capture; no regulator or statistical series corroborates the totals ([capital spending](2026-08-06-telcos-call-for-policy-consistency-regulatory-certainty-nigeria)).

summary: [Telecoms foreign direct investment](2026-02-17-telecoms-fdi-highest-since-2019) reached US$392.91m in nine months, a [fibre bond](2026-08-01-dimension-data-nigeria-fibre-bond) and an [agritech commercial paper](2026-08-25-thriveagric-commercial-paper-techcabal) raised local capital, and a [domestic seed fund closed at US$84m](2026-08-26-ventures-platform-second-fund-84m-techcabal).
developments:
Foreign direct investment in telecoms reached US$392.91m in the first nine months of 2025, the strongest since 2019 and up from a 2021 low of US$107.46m, attributed to the tariff reset and naira stability ([investment](2026-02-17-telecoms-fdi-highest-since-2019)).

A ₦4.05bn first tranche of a ₦20bn bond programme closed through a special purpose vehicle; the size is trivial against the donor lines and the financing route is the finding, long-dated local capital in a market whose rates push savings to short maturities ([bond](2026-08-01-dimension-data-nigeria-fibre-bond), [tranche](2026-07-29-dimension-data-raises-n4-05bn-broadband-bond)).

An agricultural technology company raised ₦5.3bn in the first series of an approved ₦50bn commercial paper programme, oversubscribed against a ₦5bn target ([paper](2026-08-25-thriveagric-commercial-paper-techcabal)), and a domestic seed-stage firm closed its second fund at US$84m, within US$23m of the total raised by all six African venture funds that closed in 2025 ([fund](2026-08-26-ventures-platform-second-fund-84m-techcabal)).

2026-08-26 — the manager's own release puts the second fund at [US$84m against a US$75m target, oversubscribed](2026-08-26-ventures-platform-fund-ii-final-close-release), naming a European reconstruction bank, a Norwegian development financier and a university foundation among new limited partners joining a base that already held the World Bank's private-sector arm and British and French development financiers.

summary: A [US$430m identity programme](2024-12-30 World Bank expands Nigeria's digital ID target to 180 million, extends ID4D project to 2026) runs to the end of 2026, [US$110m of startup debt](2026-07-30-fg-launches-110m-debt-financing-tech-startups-idice) opened for applications, and a [six-year country framework](2026-08-21-brandiq-world-bank-nigeria-cpf-2026-2032-broadband) puts broadband at the centre of lending.
developments:
The identity financing is US$430m from three lenders, approved in 2020 and restructured in December 2024, raising the enrolment target from 148m to 180m and extending closing to the end of 2026 ([financing](2024-12-30 World Bank expands Nigeria's digital ID target to 180 million, extends ID4D project to 2026), [restructuring](2024-12-24-worldbank-nigeria-id4d-restructuring-p167183)).

US$110m in debt financing for technology startups opened for applications in July 2026 ([debt](2026-07-30-fg-launches-110m-debt-financing-tech-startups-idice)), and a six-year country partnership framework puts electricity, broadband and private capital at the centre of the lending programme with no digital lending line itemised ([framework](2026-08-21-brandiq-world-bank-nigeria-cpf-2026-2032-broadband)).

A startup hub programme of US$51.2m runs alongside ([hub](2025-06-19-nitda-jica-startup-hub-agreement)), and a development finance institution extended US$150m for operator network upgrades ([upgrades](2026-07-07-ifc-150m-airtel-africa-digital-infrastructure)).

summary: [188m mobile subscriptions and 157m internet subscribers](2026-06-28-telecom-subs-188m-broadband-55-67) sit above [4G population coverage of about 85 per cent](2025-11-01-ncc-2024-subscriber-network-performance-report), while a [roaming remedy](2025-05-30-9mobile-roaming-mtn-network) has produced no subscriber recovery.
developments:
Two regulator series run side by side: mobile subscriptions at 188m with broadband penetration 55.67 per cent in April 2026, up from 50 per cent in November 2025, and internet subscribers at about 157m in May 2026, up 2.67m in the month ([subscriptions](2026-06-28-telecom-subs-188m-broadband-55-67)); the internet series counts active data-using lines, so reactivation and acquisition are indistinguishable in it ([subscriptions](2026-06-28-telecom-subs-188m-broadband-55-67), [internet](2026-08-04-globacom-nigeria-internet-subscriber-growth-may)).

Population coverage runs 4G at about 85 per cent and 5G at about 13 per cent against 2030 targets of at least 96 and at least 50 ([coverage](2025-11-01-ncc-2024-subscriber-network-performance-report)); 2G reaches 95.31 per cent and 3G 89.42 ([coverage](2025-11-01-ncc-2024-subscriber-network-performance-report), [roadmap](2026-03-01-ncc-spectrum-roadmap-2026-2030)).

Close to a year after national roaming was approved as a remedy, the beneficiary operator was flat at 802,534 internet subscribers for a second month ([roaming](2025-05-30-9mobile-roaming-mtn-network)), while a competitor grew from about 13,000 to about 17,200 sites in three years ([retail](2026-07-22-airtel-nigeria-retail-expansion)).

summary: [Fibre overtook fixed wireless](2026-08-25-techcabal-nigeria-fibre-internet-connectivity) for the first time with median fixed download at 34.47 Mbps, and [rural medians rose](2026-05-04-ncc-ookla-network-performance-and-connectivity-reports) on the regulator's crowdsourced measurement.
developments:
Fibre-to-the-premises connections reached 265,000 by June 2026 from 84,141 at the end of 2025, the median fixed download speed rose 155 per cent to 34.47 Mbps, uploads nearly doubled and latency fell ([mix](2026-08-25-techcabal-nigeria-fibre-internet-connectivity)); the gain sits at the bottom of the distribution, the slowest decile improving from 2.24 to 6.04 Mbps while the fastest moved only from 74.37 to 90.04 ([mix](2026-08-25-techcabal-nigeria-fibre-internet-connectivity)).

Rural median download rose from 15.0 to 16.4 Mbps and rural latency fell, on a test base growing from 266,970 to 543,123 ([measurement](2026-05-04-ncc-ookla-network-performance-and-connectivity-reports)); only 31.4 per cent of 5G-capable devices in the capital territory and 27.5 in Lagos actually use 5G, unchanged over six months, with a negative promoter score for every carrier ([measurement](2026-05-04-ncc-ookla-network-performance-and-connectivity-reports), [geospatial](2025-12-01-ncc-ookla-geospatial-precision-urban-rural-network-performance)).

One operator is live in five cities with six further states named for launch before the end of 2026 ([footprint](2026-08-24-nigeria-fiberone-seven-state-broadband-expansion)), and the largest operator is building toward a target of 8m fibre homes by 2028 ([homes](2025-10-10-mtn-8-million-homes-fibre-2028)).

summary: [Sub-US$100 smartphone shipments fell 34 per cent](2026-08-20-ai-driving-up-africa-smartphone-prices) in a quarter with the African average price up US$41, and [consumer cloud storage rose more than 50 per cent](2026-08-25-google-one-price-increase-nigeria-egypt-algeria) on some plans.
developments:
A global memory-chip shortage turns device cost into a digital-divide variable in a market that imports almost every computer it sells: sub-US$100 shipments fell 34 per cent year on year in the second quarter of 2026, the continental average selling price rose US$41 to US$202, and the Nigerian market fell 11 per cent in the quarter as buyers delayed purchases ([devices](2026-08-20-ai-driving-up-africa-smartphone-prices)); the analyst's stated cause is artificial-intelligence data-centre demand for memory making US$75 devices unprofitable to build ([devices](2026-08-20-ai-driving-up-africa-smartphone-prices), [laptops](2026-07-29-vanguard-why-laptops-more-expensive-nigeria)).

A single provider raised consumer cloud storage prices by more than 50 per cent on some plans, with Nigerian users facing increases of up to 52 per cent ([storage](2026-08-25-google-one-price-increase-nigeria-egypt-algeria)); it is the only dated consumer cloud price the base holds ([storage](2026-08-25-google-one-price-increase-nigeria-egypt-algeria)).

progress: Mixed, a 90,000 km open-access programme moving into execution while the fibre already built bypasses 130m people
summary: [Project BRIDGE](2026-08-26-nigeria-project-bridge-90000km-fibre-barriers-sun) has a US$1.6bn appraised envelope and an October 2026 start, against [about 101,000 km already built](2026-07-29-how-nigeria-built-101000km-of-fibre-that-bypasses-130m-nigerians) that bypasses some 130m Nigerians.
developments:
The programme's special purpose vehicle is incorporated with private investors at 51 to 75 per cent and the state at 25 to 49 ([execution](2026-08-10-nigeria-project-bridge-execution-phase-bridge-oa)); the minister stated in August 2026 that the 90,000 km rollout begins in October and that funding is raised, against the 2027 start for physical deployment the project documents carry ([execution](2026-08-10-nigeria-project-bridge-execution-phase-bridge-oa), [rollout](2026-08-20-punch-nigeria-project-bridge-fibre-october), [envelope](2026-08-04-nigeria-project-bridge-fibre-spv)).

The financier's own two figures are five weeks apart and on different bases: an appraisal counting 30,000 km of terrestrial fibre deployed against the 120,000 km the national blueprint requires and stating flatly that there is no national backbone network, and a board statement framing the programme as extending the backbone from 35,000 km to 125,000 ([appraisal](2025-09-08-world-bank-bridge-nigeria-project-appraisal-document), [approval](2025-10-07-world-bank-approves-bridge-nigeria-digital-health-security)).

About 101,000 km of fibre has been built and the finding is that it bypasses some 130m Nigerians, a utilisation and last-mile problem rather than a backbone one ([utilisation](2026-07-29-how-nigeria-built-101000km-of-fibre-that-bypasses-130m-nigerians)); an operator lit a 400G and 800G optical backbone in October 2025 ([optical](2025-10-22-mtn-huawei-400g-800g-optical-network)).

summary: The [national internet exchange passed 1 Tbps](2025-04-24-ixpn-1tbps-traffic-milestone) of traffic in April 2025, and [close to twelve licence-exempt optical links](2026-08-11-taara-and-liquid-use-light-beam-technology-to-expand-data-centre-capacity-to-lar) now carry urban transport across Lagos.
developments:
The exchange passed a 1 Tbps traffic milestone in April 2025 ([exchange](2025-04-24-ixpn-1tbps-traffic-milestone)).

Two companies say they deployed close to twelve wireless optical links across Lagos over two years, distributing bandwidth from points of presence to banks, internet providers, hotels and a utility, rated at up to 20 Gbps over up to 20 km, with three further cities named next; the links need no trenching, civil works or spectrum licence, so a high-capacity urban transport layer sits outside the spectrum instruments the regulator uses to shape the market ([links](2026-08-11-taara-and-liquid-use-light-beam-technology-to-expand-data-centre-capacity-to-lar), [deployment](2026-08-05-taara-liquid-wireless-connectivity-nigeria)).

progress: Mixed, the largest satellite provider paused orders over congestion and was brought inside biometric verification while three further satellite programmes remain unbuilt
summary: [Satellite service became the second-largest provider](2025-03-10-starlink-second-largest-isp) then paused orders over congestion, a [second landing permit](2026-01-15-ncc-amazon-kuiper-landing-permit) was granted with no service, and [two national satellites](2026-08-24-nigeria-iai-thales-alenia-space-deux-satellites-wearetech) were approved for 2028 and beyond.
developments:
The incumbent satellite service became the country's second-largest internet provider on late-2024 figures, then paused new orders in parts of two cities over congestion in September 2025, and was brought inside the regulator's biometric subscriber-verification regime with more than 66,000 users required to submit identity numbers and headshots ([provider](2025-03-10-starlink-second-largest-isp), [congestion](2025-09-15-starlink-halts-orders-congestion), [verification](2025-12-31-starlink-biometric-66000-subscribers)).

A landing permit for a second constellation was granted in January 2026 with no service ([permit](2026-01-15-ncc-amazon-kuiper-landing-permit)).

Cabinet approved the acquisition of two high-throughput communications satellites in August 2026 on an operator timetable of 2028 and 2029 or 2030, with no contract value published and negotiation still to follow ([satellites](2026-08-24-nigeria-iai-thales-alenia-space-deux-satellites-wearetech), [approval](2026-08-22-saharareporters-nigcomsat-2a-2b-approval)); a low-earth-orbit partnership announced in January 2025 has no service ([partnership](2025-01-20-nigcomsat-eutelsat-leo-services)) and a direct-to-device memorandum targeted for end-2025 has nothing on file ([direct to device](2025-06-20-nasrda-galaxy-space-d2d-satellite)).

summary: About [26 facilities carry 50 to 56 MW of declared live capacity](2026-07-07 CBN's local data order puts Nigeria's data centres to test) on one count and about 28 MW on another, with a [US$250m hyperscale campus](2026-05-28-kasi-cloud-los1-hyperscale-flagoff) and a [4.5 MW operator facility](2025-07-01 MTN launches West Africa's largest Tier III data centre with cloud services (Techpoint)) among the builds.
developments:
One trade tracker maps about 26 facilities, eighteen of them commercial colocation, at about 50 to 56 MW of declared live capacity rising to about 124 MW when design specifications are counted; an independent research house measuring capacity active, under lease or readily available puts it at about 28 MW across about fifteen live facilities against about 80 MW at full build. The two counts are not reconcilable without their definitions, and the country is Africa's second-largest market at about 15 per cent of continental capacity ([estate](2026-07-07 CBN's local data order puts Nigeria's data centres to test), [briefing](2026-01-01-xalam-nigeria-data-center-market-briefing)).

A US$250m campus backed by the sovereign wealth fund is in build toward about 100 MW ([campus](2026-05-28-kasi-cloud-los1-hyperscale-flagoff)), an operator's first phase runs 4.5 MW and 780 racks scaling to 9-14 MW ([operator](2025-07-01 MTN launches West Africa's largest Tier III data centre with cloud services (Techpoint))), a colocation facility is expanding to 24 MW by 2027 ([expansion](2025-03-24 Open Access Data Centres to expand Lagos facility to 24MW by 2027)), a 2 MW facility opened in Lagos in 2025 ([facility](2025-08-25 Digital Realty launches a 2MW data center (LKK2) in Lagos, Nigeria)), and a second operator announced a 38 MW build of more than 3,000 racks at over US$120m ([build](2025-08-08 Airtel Nigeria to build 38MW hyperscale data centre in Eko Atlantic (Nxtra))).

summary: The sovereign wealth fund announced a 100MW hyperscale data centre campus in Lagos ([announcement](2026-09-01-nsia-kasi-100mw-ai-data-centre-nigeria)).
developments:
The sovereign wealth fund announced a 100MW artificial-intelligence-ready hyperscale campus in Lagos, offering co-location, cloud, storage and high-performance compute ([announcement](2026-09-01-nsia-kasi-100mw-ai-data-centre-nigeria)). It is announced, not built: no construction start, cost or completion date is stated.

The government cloud delivers document storage, mail, content management and electronic signature through the state infrastructure company across ministries ([cloud](2025-09-10-1gov-cloud-galaxy-backbone)).

The sovereign cloud initiative's implementation taskforce was inaugurated in August 2026 to align regulators, institutions and private operators behind technical standards, cloud governance, infrastructure assurance and investment frameworks; Nigerian organisations are estimated to spend about US$850m a year on foreign cloud infrastructure against a policy target of US$750m in private investment within 24 months, and how the taskforce relates to a joint technical committee inaugurated four days earlier is not established ([initiative](2026-08-25-nitda-national-sovereign-cloud-taskforce), [taskforce](2026-08-25-nigeria-national-cloud-taskforce-itweb)).

A pan-African operator's national sovereign cloud went live in March 2026 ([operator cloud](2026-03-05 Cassava AI - Cassava Technologies announces National Sovereign Cloud to support secure digital infrastructure for African governments)), subsidised sovereign cloud opened for startups in May 2026 ([subsidy](2026-05-05-gbb-ondi-subsidised-sovereign-cloud-startups)), and one sovereign-cloud build rides partly on a Chinese stack ([stack](2026-06-10-21st-century-china-mobile-sovereign-cloud)).

summary: A [Lagos cloud region](2026-08-10-africloud-lagos-cloud-region-nigeria) gives one platform three separate legal jurisdictions, and an [edge facility](2026-01-08 Nigeria's digital future gets a boost with Fringe's Ikoyi Metro EDGE launch) opened in January 2026.
developments:
The Lagos region is a full compute region in a carrier-neutral facility, the third alongside two others, framed around data residency since the data protection Act took effect and giving three separate legal jurisdictions across the platform ([region](2026-08-10-africloud-lagos-cloud-region-nigeria)).

An edge facility entered service in January 2026 ([edge](2026-01-08 Nigeria's digital future gets a boost with Fringe's Ikoyi Metro EDGE launch)). No disaster-recovery arrangement, replication rule or backup requirement for government systems is published anywhere in this base.

summary: The [grid has never reliably exceeded 6 GW](2026-05-21 Africa Data Center Investment 2026 The $4.5B Race and the Power Problem) for about 230m people, while an operator venture targets [150 MW in a first phase](2026-08-25-techcentral-mtn-150mw-first-phase-ai-data-centre) spanning two countries.
developments:
Grid availability runs at roughly 41 per cent, diesel backup costs US$0.40 to US$0.50 a kilowatt-hour against US$0.05 to US$0.10 on the grid in two comparable markets and adds about 40 per cent to operating cost, and construction runs about US$12 a watt ([grid](2026-05-21 Africa Data Center Investment 2026 The $4.5B Race and the Power Problem)).

A Gulf-backed venture in which the operator group holds a minority stake targets 150 MW in a first phase spanning South Africa and Nigeria; no Nigerian site, split, cost or commissioning date is stated ([venture](2026-08-25-techcentral-mtn-150mw-first-phase-ai-data-centre)). Announced compute capacity is being planned against a grid that cannot presently carry it.

summary: The communications regulator and the [rural electrification agency signed a data-sharing memorandum](2026-07-29-ncc-rea-sign-mou-to-drive-digital-infrastructure-expansion) overlaying electrification and universal-service deployment data.
developments: The agency supplies geospatial electrification data and the regulator its universal service fund deployment data, overlaid to find joint connectivity-and-energy gaps; it is the first Nigerian instrument to treat rural electrification and connectivity planning data as one dataset, and no amount, timeline or funding source is stated ([memorandum](2026-07-29-ncc-rea-sign-mou-to-drive-digital-infrastructure-expansion)).

progress: Mixed, a payroll and human-resource platform live across 508 agencies while the identity platform is not sized for the compulsory use the new Act requires
summary: [Human-resource modules](2026-07-27-fg-launches-ippis-human-resource-modules) run across more than 508 agencies and 600,000 civil servants, while the [identity platform is not sized](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act) for compulsory use across fourteen sectors.
developments:
The modules cover biometric onboarding, establishment management, payroll administration, mobility, self-service and workforce analytics, migrated to a locally built platform and placed under a domestic-first policy as strengthening the sovereignty of government personnel data ([modules](2026-07-27-fg-launches-ippis-human-resource-modules)).

Servers, databases and networks are not sized for compulsory use of the identity number across the fourteen sectors the amended Act reaches, and a compulsory register carries an election-integrity risk if it cannot be relied on ([capacity](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act)).

summary: [155,397 fibre cuts in two months](2026-08-04-nigeria-project-bridge-fibre-spv) with more than 54,000 attributed to vandalism, [more than 5,000 cuts from road works](2026-08-11-nigeria-ncc-fibre-cuts-road-works) in a half-year, and a [standing protection committee](2026-08-11-nigeria-ncc-fibre-cuts-road-works) with no published powers.
developments:
Cuts ran at 155,397 across April and May 2026 alone against 19,384 cuts, 3,241 equipment thefts and more than 19,000 site-access denials across January to August 2025, an order-of-magnitude deterioration recorded despite the critical-infrastructure order gazetted in 2024 ([vandalism](2026-07-29-vanguard-telecom-operators-infrastructure-protection)); operators name vandalism, multiple taxation and right-of-way as the constraints on network quality rather than regulatory penalties ([vandalism](2026-07-29-vanguard-telecom-operators-infrastructure-protection), [cuts](2025-10-08-ncc-19000-fibre-cuts-eight-months)).

The regulator separately counted more than 5,000 cuts from road works in the first half of 2026 ([road works](2026-08-11-nigeria-ncc-fibre-cuts-road-works)).

A standing committee was formed with two ministries and the security adviser's office to coordinate protection of fibre designated critical national information infrastructure, with no terms of reference, meeting cycle, budget or enforcement power published ([committee](2026-08-11-nigeria-ncc-fibre-cuts-road-works)).

summary: A [Cyber Resilience Framework](2026-02-23-cyber-resilience-framework-nigeria-communication-sector-crf-ncs) binds every licensed provider on a clock ending February 2027 with four-hour incident notification, and the [police cybercrime centre](2025-01-09-nigeria-police-cybercrime-unit-interpol) recovered ₦8.82bn in 2024.
developments:
The framework took effect in February 2026 and stages compliance in three tiers at six, nine and twelve months, running on five pillars with coded standards, tiering providers by network and sector role, placing accountability on boards and executive management, and binding to the data protection Act and the critical-infrastructure order; a guidance note of August 2026 adds a dedicated cybersecurity budget line, a chief information security officer and two-year in-country retention of call logs and traffic data ([framework](2026-02-23-cyber-resilience-framework-nigeria-communication-sector-crf-ncs), [notification](2026-03-05-ncc-4-hour-cyber-incident-reporting-crf), [budgets](2026-08-07-nigerian-mandates-telco-cybersecurity-budgets)).

The police cybercrime centre was named the best African unit for 2024, recovering ₦8.82bn and arresting more than 751 suspects ([police](2025-01-09-nigeria-police-cybercrime-unit-interpol)).

A ministerial advisory council was announced with no membership or terms of reference published ([council](2026-08-04-nigeria-now-west-africas-digital-powerhouse-says-tijani)), and a bilateral partnership is rated more than 90 per cent implemented by the national coordinator, credited with the continent's first four certified incident-response auditors ([partnership](2026-08-22-businessday-nigeria-uk-cyber-alliance-ai-threats)).

summary: The [national data exchange](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services) is moving personal data in production with no lawful basis on record, and practitioners describe the identity layer as [federated linkage rather than integration](2026-07-25-nin-contradiction-high-cost-of-false-integration).
developments:
The exchange was built with European partners to end an eight-siloed-database problem and now moves personal data between agencies in production behind the government service portal; the lawful basis and audit arrangements for that sharing are unstated ([exchange](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services), [launch](2025-08-28 Nigeria to launch National Data Exchange (NGDX) platform to boost digital economy)).

Named practitioners describe the identity number as a federated linkage system with a shared identifier rather than a fully integrated identity system, with banks still reconciling manually and buying third-party verification interfaces; this qualifies a single-source-of-truth framing stated three days earlier and neither source reconciles the two ([linkage](2026-07-25-nin-contradiction-high-cost-of-false-integration), [fragmentation](2026-07-15-nigeria-national-database-still-fragmented)).

A state is building a single patient-data platform connecting records, laboratory results and biological data across facilities, with no legal basis, controller arrangement, consent model or relationship to the national regime stated ([health platform](2026-08-08-nigeria-lagos-ship-ai-health-data-interoperability)).

summary: [Nine agencies took bilateral integration cover](2026-07-22-thisday-shettima-digital-transformation-nimc-act-2026) under the new identity Act in a fortnight, a [telecom identity feed](2026-04-21-cbn-ncc-tirms-telecom-data-banks) lets banks check SIM swaps, and the number is [tied to health insurance records](2025-10-10-nimc-nhia-digital-id-health-mou).
developments:
Nine agencies concluded bilateral commitments across a single fortnight, and the electoral commission's chairman acknowledged the Act as a legal basis for resolving duplicate identities in the voter register; no account states a lawful basis, consent mechanism, retention rule or regulator role for the resulting sharing ([agreements](2026-07-22-thisday-shettima-digital-transformation-nimc-act-2026), [partnerships](2026-07-24-thisday-nimc-partnerships-women-affairs-boi-digital-identity)).

A joint feed between the central bank and the communications regulator lets banks check SIM-swap and recycled numbers before clearing, and fraud fell 51 per cent to ₦25.85bn in 2025 ([feed](2026-04-21-cbn-ncc-tirms-telecom-data-banks)).

The identity number was tied to health insurance records in October 2025 ([health](2025-10-10-nimc-nhia-digital-id-health-mou)).

progress: Mixed, registrations at 136m against a 180m target while corrections are confined to a portal the majority of adults cannot reach
summary: [136m registrations](2026-07-09 NIMC Enrols 136 Million Nigerians as Coker-Odusote Pushes Stronger Inter-Ministerial Partnership) stand against a 180m target for end-2026 with about 100m still uncaptured, and [corrections are confined to a smartphone portal](2026-03-29 When digital identity fails the citizen Who bears responsibility for NIN suspensions) excluding about 72 per cent of adults.
developments:
Registrations passed 136m by July 2026 from 123.9m in October 2025, against a target of 180m by the end of 2026; about 100m people are still uncaptured on the information minister's own figure, and enrolment runs 56.25 per cent male to 43.75 per cent female ([registrations](2026-07-09 NIMC Enrols 136 Million Nigerians as Coker-Odusote Pushes Stronger Inter-Ministerial Partnership), [enrolment](2026-06-05 Nigeria looks beyond enrollment as digital ID passes 130 million), [count](2025-12-18 NIN enrollments hit 123.9 million in October 2025 - NIMC)).

A 2024 policy confined corrections to a device-locked smartphone self-service portal, excluding the about 72 per cent of adults without smartphones and enabling agent charges of ₦12,000 to ₦62,000 against an official ₦2,000 ([corrections](2026-03-29 When digital identity fails the citizen Who bears responsibility for NIN suspensions)); validly issued numbers are also being suspended over enrolment-centre bypass with reinstatement fees pushed onto citizens ([corrections](2026-03-29 When digital identity fails the citizen Who bears responsibility for NIN suspensions), [regime](2026-03-07 Nigerians Groan Under Digital Identity Regime That Turns Basic Rights into Privileges)).

summary: A [ward-level drive](2026-02-16 Nigeria launches nationwide ward-level drive to boost digital ID coverage and inclusion) opened free enrolment across all 8,809 wards, against a [22.3-point gender gap](2026-01-28 The Gender Gap in Rural Niger State's Digital Identity) in who holds an identity number.
developments:
Free enrolment runs in every ward across the 774 local government areas, targeting women, children, elderly people, persons with disabilities and refugees ([drive](2026-02-16 Nigeria launches nationwide ward-level drive to boost digital ID coverage and inclusion), [progress](2026-03-04 NIMC Intensifies Ward-Level NIN Enrolment Nationwide)).

Women are 38.8 per cent of enrolled holders against 61.1 per cent men, a 22.3-point gap ([gap](2026-01-28 The Gender Gap in Rural Niger State's Digital Identity)); in one state twenty-one centres serve about 7.5m people, a ₦3,000 round trip is prohibitive, no number means no access to the maternal-care fund, and rural women's phone ownership is 42 per cent against 78 urban ([gap](2026-01-28 The Gender Gap in Rural Niger State's Digital Identity)). The drive is aimed squarely at that gap and no post-drive gender figure is published.

summary: [Consent-based verification](2025-05-07 Nigeria unveils NINAuth platform to streamline national ID authentication and verification) went live in May 2025, the identity commission [holds the national root certification authority](2026-08-13-nigeria-s-identity-law-raises-questions-over-who-regulates-digital-signatures), and [airport identity verification](2026-07-21-nigeria-nimc-new-duties-digital-ecosystem) runs on number and face.
developments:
Consent-based verification launched in May 2025 ([verification](2025-05-07 Nigeria unveils NINAuth platform to streamline national ID authentication and verification)).

The root certification authority role was handed over from the technology agency, with the wider partnership formalised in July 2026 covering the key-infrastructure transfer and harmonised digital-trust standards; it creates an overlap with the electronic-signature provisions of the still-pending economy bill, and which instrument governs digital signatures is unresolved ([overlap](2026-08-13-nigeria-s-identity-law-raises-questions-over-who-regulates-digital-signatures), [duties](2026-07-21-nigeria-nimc-new-duties-digital-ecosystem), [certification](2026-07-16-nimc-digital-signature-certification-authority)).

Travellers enrol identity number and face biometrics for digital security checks and boarding ([airport](2026-07-21-nigeria-nimc-new-duties-digital-ecosystem)).

summary: A [multipurpose biometric card](2025-01-27-multiuse-biometric-id-card-launch) is in development with the payments switch, a [cooperative identity credential](2026-08-13-nigeria-cooperative-digital-id-mou) is in revalidation, and [border management](2026-08-25-dailyasset-nigeria-nis-digital-border-management) is being biometrically strengthened.
developments:
The three-in-one biometric card with multiple wallets is in development with the payments switch and the domestic card scheme, for agency services, student loans and farmer inputs ([card](2025-01-27-multiuse-biometric-id-card-launch), [memorandum](2025-03-08-nimc-nelfund-biometric-cards-mou)).

A six-month revalidation exercise is under way to issue cooperatives a verification number and their members an identity credential under a memorandum with a private identity supplier; no cooperative or member count, cost, or link to the foundational register is stated ([cooperatives](2026-08-13-nigeria-cooperative-digital-id-mou)).

Border management is being strengthened through digital technology, biometric identity systems and intelligence sharing, on a statement at a forum rather than a procurement, with no system, vendor, cost or data-protection arrangement for the biometric collection stated ([borders](2026-08-25-dailyasset-nigeria-nis-digital-border-management)).

summary: A [learner identification number](2026-08-05-nigeria-integrates-national-student-ids-digital-identity-system) was integrated with the identity register, [farmer verification](2026-07-12 Agric Ministry adopts NIMC identity system to verify genuine farmers) is planned on a subsidy taper, a [credit bureau](2025-06-17-credicorp-nin-credit-scores-bureau) would key scores to the number, and [pre-registered SIMs ended](2025-11-11-ncc-end-pre-registered-sim-regulations).
developments:
A sixteen-digit learner number issued from April 2026 reached 1.9m at launch and was integrated with the identity register across a stated 80m student records; birth registration is integrated so newly registered children receive a number automatically, yet school admission remains manual and the birth register is not connected to any state education platform, so the failure is interoperability rather than enrolment. The integration was announced on a social platform rather than in an instrument, and it makes school enrolment an enrolment channel for the identity register ([learners](2026-08-05-nigeria-integrates-national-student-ids-digital-identity-system), [gap](2026-07-31-nigeria-digital-identity-gap-leaves-schoolchildren-behind)).

A centralised farmers database would target subsidies on a three-year taper and remove ghost beneficiaries ([farmers](2026-07-12 Agric Ministry adopts NIMC identity system to verify genuine farmers)), and a proposed bureau would tie credit scores to the number with consequences for defaulters extending to passport and licence renewal and tenancy ([credit](2025-06-17-credicorp-nin-credit-scores-bureau)).

Pre-registered cards ended in November 2025 ([cards](2025-11-11-ncc-end-pre-registered-sim-regulations)).

summary: A [Payments System Vision 2028](2026-06-17-cbn-nigeria-payments-system-vision-2028) sets 95 per cent inclusion and a 70 per cent fraud cut from a ₦1.2 quadrillion baseline, alongside [market-concentration caps](2026-07-20-cbn-rewriting-rules-nigeria-fintech-growth), a [foreign-exchange tracker](2026-07-17-nigeria-central-bank-digitises-forex-oversight) and a [second sandbox cohort](2026-08-13-nigeria-cbn-sandbox-cohort-2-itweb).
developments:
The vision runs a three-year horizon from 2025 baselines of ₦1.2 quadrillion in electronic transactions, 5.9m active terminals and 69.5m unique identifiers, targeting 95 per cent financial inclusion, full interoperability, adult digital-payment usage from about 52 to 80 per cent, 5m code-based merchant outlets and a 70 per cent reduction in fraud losses ([vision](2026-06-17-cbn-nigeria-payments-system-vision-2028), [launch](2026-06-01-cbn-payments-system-vision-2028-launch)).

Any institution above 25 per cent of consumer issuing may not exceed 15 per cent of merchant acquiring and the reverse, on monthly market-share returns with compliance by end-2026 ([caps](2026-07-20-cbn-rewriting-rules-nigeria-fintech-growth)).

Every licensed foreign-exchange bureau must report purchases in real time or same-day with banks as first line of enforcement ([tracker](2026-07-17-nigeria-central-bank-digitises-forex-oversight)); a second sandbox cohort opened to virtual-asset and data-enabled firms ([sandbox](2026-08-13-nigeria-cbn-sandbox-cohort-2-itweb)); and the retail digital currency is being redesigned toward a wholesale model rather than abandoned ([currency](2026-07-26-nigeria-payment-vision-2028)).

summary: [Instant payments reached US$256bn](2025-10-09-nigeria-e-payments-256bn-cbn) across 4.12bn transactions, a [National Payment Stack](2026-08-12-nigeria-nibss-national-payment-stack-iso20022) carries 26.55m transactions on the new standard, and [short-code billing](2025-06-11-ussd-end-user-billing-model) settled a multi-year dispute.
developments:
Electronic payments reached US$256bn by July 2025 from US$187bn a year earlier across 4.12bn transactions, and the instant system was rated the first African instant system to achieve mature inclusivity ([payments](2025-10-09-nigeria-e-payments-256bn-cbn), [rating](2025-12-23-siips-nigeria-instant-payments-2tn)).

The successor stack reports 26.55 million transactions worth ₦1.4 trillion across 48 institutions in its early phase, on a multi-currency platform carrying payments, identity and data together, with its first live transaction in November 2025 ([stack](2026-08-12-nigeria-nibss-national-payment-stack-iso20022), [first transaction](2025-11-10-nibss-national-payment-stack-first-transaction)).

Short-code session costs are billed to airtime at ₦6.98 per 120 seconds with real-time confirmation and opt-in, ending the multi-year operator and bank debt dispute ([billing](2025-06-11-ussd-end-user-billing-model)).

summary: [Open banking](2025-04-29-cbn-open-banking-august-launch) was mandated from August 2025 across about 120m bank customers, a payments company gained [direct card-network access without a bank sponsor](2026-08-13-nigeria-teamapt-mastercard-network-access), and [embedded insurance](2026-07-17-skydd-insure-fintech-leadership) opened to institutions.
developments:
Open banking was the first in Africa, mandating consented customer-data sharing across about 120m bank customers through identifier-tied consent, a central registry and standardised interfaces, four years after the framework ([open banking](2025-04-29-cbn-open-banking-august-launch)).

A Nigerian payments company gained direct access to a global card network as a non-bank acquirer, letting it onboard licensed merchants without a bank sponsor; no merchant count, pricing or settlement arrangement is stated ([access](2026-08-13-nigeria-teamapt-mastercard-network-access)).

Tier-one banks hold payments infrastructure inside the group rather than at arm's length, and the central bank has begun regulating fintech ownership as well as conduct ([ownership](2026-08-02-techtrends-african-corporate-venture-capital-banks)); embedded insurance infrastructure opened to banks, fintechs, employers and merchants ([insurance](2026-07-17-skydd-insure-fintech-leadership)).

progress: Mixed, wallet revenue and retail investing rising while point-of-sale volumes fell a fifth under new agent-banking limits
summary: [Point-of-sale volumes fell 19.9 per cent](2026-08-17-nigerians-returning-to-atms-pos-falls) as cash machine use rose, [operator wallet revenue rose about 132 per cent](2026-08-25-mtn-nigeria-30-million-fintech-users-techcabal), and [financial inclusion stood at 74 per cent](2026-07-26-nigeria-payment-vision-2028) against a 95 target.
developments:
Cash machine transactions rose 6.6 per cent year on year in the first quarter of 2026 with value up 64.6 per cent, while point-of-sale volumes fell 19.9 per cent to 2.92bn ([mix](2026-08-17-nigerians-returning-to-atms-pos-falls)); agent-banking limits imposed in October 2025, single-provider terminals, a seventy-metre radius rule and a daily cap constrained the agent channel as the central bank pushed bank machine expansion, and the record carries no measure of what the limits did to access where there is no branch ([mix](2026-08-17-nigerians-returning-to-atms-pos-falls)).

Operator wallet revenue grew about 132 per cent in the first half of 2026 with active wallets up 1.3m to 5m, against a medium-term target of 30 million ([wallets](2026-08-25-mtn-nigeria-30-million-fintech-users-techcabal), [slump](2026-07-31-mtn-nigeria-fintech-revenue-slump)).

Inclusion stood at 74 per cent in 2023 against a 95 per cent target for 2028 ([inclusion](2026-07-26-nigeria-payment-vision-2028)), and retail investors traded ₦2.86tn of equities in five months, up 138.76 per cent ([investing](2026-07-18-nigeria-retail-investing-boom)).

summary: [Continental rail flows fell 53 per cent](2026-01-27 Nigeria's PAPSS cross-border payments falls 53% to N5.6bn) to about US$3.7m in a half-year, while [stablecoin settlement rails](2026-07-20-busha-business-tether-stablecoin-infrastructure-africa) carry 1,500 businesses and a [regulated naira stablecoin](2026-08-12-nigeria-cngn-stablecoin-celo-blockchain) went live on a public blockchain.
developments:
A commercial bank put the continental payment system on its app and online channels with no separate onboarding, capped at the local-currency equivalent of US$2,000 a month for individuals ([report](2026-08-26-papss-firstbank-payment-rails-starconnect)).

Flows on the continental rail fell 53 per cent to ₦5.6bn in the first half of 2025 with transactions down 29 per cent to 3,246 ([rail](2026-01-27 Nigeria's PAPSS cross-border payments falls 53% to N5.6bn)); at about US$3.7m for a half-year that reads as a narrow line item rather than national throughput, and the country remains the rail's largest participant ([rail](2026-01-27 Nigeria's PAPSS cross-border payments falls 53% to N5.6bn)). A wallet-based corridor to Ghana entered pilot ([corridor](2026-02-04-onafriq-papss-naira-wallet-ghana)).

A licensed local exchange plugged into a dollar stablecoin's liquidity for cross-border settlement, reporting more than 1,500 businesses across two countries ([rails](2026-07-20-busha-business-tether-stablecoin-infrastructure-africa)); the yield partners and rates are undisclosed ([rails](2026-07-20-busha-business-tether-stablecoin-infrastructure-africa), [settlement](2026-07-21-stablecoins-test-africas-monetary-future)).

The regulated naira stablecoin went live on a public blockchain in August 2026 backed one-to-one, with no supply, holder count or reserve attestation published ([token](2026-08-12-nigeria-cngn-stablecoin-celo-blockchain), [listing](2025-02-10-busha-lists-cngn-stablecoin)); remote diaspora bank onboarding launched in 2025 as remittances rose from US$3.3bn to US$4.73bn ([diaspora](2025-05-13-cbn-diaspora-nrbvn-platform)).

progress: Mixed, fraud losses halved on a falling reporting rate while a digital-lending regime went to appeal and forty million airtime borrowers sat between two regulators
summary: [Fraud losses fell 51 per cent](2026-08-02-nigerias-digital-economy-faces-trust-test) on a reporting rate down 34 per cent, the [digital-lending regulations](2025-09-04-fccpc-deon-digital-lending-regulations) are under appeal, and [about 40m airtime borrowers](2026-08-24-mtn-nigeria-airtime-lending-rebound-techcabal) sit inside the jurisdiction dispute.
developments:
Fraud losses fell to ₦25.85bn in 2025, down 51 per cent, on 67,518 incidents against 123,918 in 2021, with fraud reporting down 34 per cent in the fourth quarter ([trust](2026-08-02-nigerias-digital-economy-faces-trust-test), [challenge](2026-07-29-why-trust-has-become-nigeria-digital-payments-challenge)).

The digital consumer-lending regulations were suspended by injunction, upheld in July 2026 and enforcement resumed, with an association's appeal before the Court of Appeal; the two regulators' positions are unreconciled, one holding airtime credit a telecommunications value-added service and the other framing the regulations as its answer to harassment and data breaches, and the communications minister has directed that the existing framework stays in place, an interim settlement by direction rather than by instrument ([regulations](2025-09-04-fccpc-deon-digital-lending-regulations), [court](2026-07-21-nigeria-court-deon-digital-lending-fccpc-ncc), [resumption](2026-07-22-fccpc-deon-digital-lending-resumes)).

The product at the centre of it reaches about 40 million users on an industry sizing of ₦300-400bn a year, and one operator resumed at about a quarter of its first-quarter run rate at a stated cost of about ₦50bn to first-half revenue ([airtime](2026-08-24-mtn-nigeria-airtime-lending-rebound-techcabal)). A payment security operations centre is a 2028 target with no legal basis or funding line ([centre](2026-07-26-nigeria-payment-vision-2028)), and a domestic cyber-insurance market is still forming ([insurance](2025-02-27-local-cyber-insurance-products)).

summary: [NGN 27.1 trillion was collected](2026-08-11-techcabal-nigeria-tax-collection-digital-systems) between January and July 2026, credited to digitised systems, with a [treasury system](2025-03-06-treasury-management-system-launch) deducting automatically and [7.5 per cent VAT on electronic banking fees](2026-01-15-fg-7-5-vat-electronic-banking).
developments:
Collection ran at NGN 27.1 trillion between January and July 2026, an average NGN 127.83bn a day and 95.76 per cent of the whole of 2025's collection, which the revenue service credits to digitised tax systems, four reform laws and an executive order closing loopholes ([collection](2026-08-11-techcabal-nigeria-tax-collection-digital-systems)); the attribution is the service's own and no counterfactual or system-level breakdown is published ([collection](2026-08-11-techcabal-nigeria-tax-collection-digital-systems)).

The treasury management and revenue assurance system automatically deducts and remits value-added tax, withholding tax and stamp duty on vendor payments across all agencies ([treasury](2025-03-06-treasury-management-system-launch)).

Value-added tax of 7.5 per cent on electronic banking fees took effect in January 2026 ([tax](2026-01-15-fg-7-5-vat-electronic-banking)).

summary: Two [2025 tax statutes](2026-01-12-tin-nin-crypto-tax-carf) underpin a [virtual-asset tax framework](2026-08-03-nigeria-crypto-stamp-duty-bitcoin-usdt) withholding 1.5 per cent in the asset itself, and a state is testing [withholding on creator payouts](2026-08-14-the-selar-row-shows-how-nigeria-plans-to-tax-its-creator-economy).
developments:
