The two 2025 statutes are the base for the virtual-asset circular and for tying crypto trades to tax and identity numbers ([statutes](2026-01-12-tin-nin-crypto-tax-carf)).

The circular imposes a 1.5 per cent stamp duty withheld in the asset itself and remitted in the originating token, so the federal government now holds token receipts and the price risk on its own tax revenue, alongside withholding on disposal proceeds, on staking and yield, value-added tax on service fees and companies income tax ([framework](2026-08-03-nigeria-crypto-stamp-duty-bitcoin-usdt)); traders warned the charge could push activity into unregulated channels, and a true wallet-to-wallet trade has no collection agent at all ([framework](2026-08-03-nigeria-crypto-stamp-duty-bitcoin-usdt), [objections](2026-08-14-nigeria-wants-to-tax-crypto-traders-say-it-could-slow-business)).

A state revenue service is testing whether creator-economy platform payouts are royalties subject to 5 per cent withholding and pressing two platforms to deduct at source ([creators](2026-08-14-the-selar-row-shows-how-nigeria-plans-to-tax-its-creator-economy)); no assessment, ruling or judgment is published ([creators](2026-08-14-the-selar-row-shows-how-nigeria-plans-to-tax-its-creator-economy)).

progress: Mixed, paper registration discontinued nationwide while the health-facility layer recorded zero birth notifications
summary: [Paper registration was discontinued](2026-07-22-npc-nationwide-digital-birth-death-registration) from July 2026, but none of 371 targeted health facilities is live, [120,469 certificates were issued against 443,162 registrations](2026-08-22-vanguard-nigeria-birth-registration-gap), and the platform showed charges for documents stated to be free.
developments:
Registration went nationwide on a single platform through 4,011 centres toward a target of about 8,000, with newborn registration requiring at least one parent to hold a valid identity number and the register run as a public-private partnership ([platform](2026-07-22-npc-nationwide-digital-birth-death-registration), [state](2026-07-23-akwa-ibom-digital-civil-registration-system)).

It has stalled at the health-facility layer: none of 371 targeted facilities is live despite completed training, zero birth notifications were recorded in the reporting year, 120,469 certificates were issued against 443,162 registrations, and an estimated 3.5 million children across seven southern states hold no certificate ([gap](2026-08-22-vanguard-nigeria-birth-registration-gap)).

The platform displayed charges of US$30 to US$80 for documents the commission says are free, and carried one man's record with a wife and a son unknown to him until the commission corrected it free of charge the day after publication ([corrections](2026-08-18-fij-npc-corrects-vitalreg-records), [records](2026-08-16-fij-npc-vitalreg-wrong-family-records)).

summary: A [national alphanumeric postcode](2026-08-04-nigeria-90000km-fibre-optic-rollout-tijani) has a launch date of 1 October 2026, and the [addressing council ratified a framework](2026-08-25-thisday-nac-framework-nigeria-digitised-addressing-system) replacing the 2017 policy.
developments:
The postcode is explicitly property-level rather than cluster-level, with integration to existing government identity databases to follow; no lawful basis, custodian or data-protection arrangement for that integration is stated ([postcode](2026-08-04-nigeria-90000km-fibre-optic-rollout-tijani)).

The council, chaired by the Vice-President, ratified a preliminary framework naming the science ministry as secretariat and assigning individual verification to the identity commission, business address verification to the corporate registry, postcode administration to the postal service and implementation to states; it would replace a 2017 standard described as obsolete, focused on mail delivery and silent on business address verification ([framework](2026-08-25-thisday-nac-framework-nigeria-digitised-addressing-system), [standard](2017-07-01-nipost-nigerian-national-addressing-standard-and-guidelines)).

A state is separately piloting digital house-numbering ([pilot](2025-06-25-lagos-digital-house-numbering-identity-project)).

summary: [More than 90 per cent of land is unregistered](2025-03-20-fg-land-information-system-digitisation), locking an estimated US$300bn as dead capital, while a [mortgage registry](2026-07-28-housing-stakeholders-validate-national-housing-data) is described as ready for deployment.
developments:
The national land registration and documentation programme is under way against more than 90 per cent of land unregistered, on the housing minister's figure ([programme](2025-03-20-fg-land-information-system-digitisation)).

A national mortgage registry is described as ready for deployment with no launch date, custodian arrangement or data-protection basis stated, and its governing policy is still a draft under stakeholder validation ([registry](2026-07-28-housing-stakeholders-validate-national-housing-data)).

One state has a live compensation and valuation land system ([state system](2025-02-04-kaduna-land-administration-software)).

summary: A [beneficial ownership register](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025) launched in 2023 is in use by enforcement agencies, alongside a [national electronic assets register](2025-03-07-national-electronic-assets-register) live since March 2025.
developments:
The [electronic assets register went live in March 2025](2025-03-07-national-electronic-assets-register); no asset count, agency coverage or update cycle is published.

The [beneficial ownership register, launched in 2023, is open to government institutions, civil society, journalists and citizens, and regulatory and enforcement agencies are using it for transparency, enforcement and asset recovery](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025); it is named as contributing to Nigeria's exit from the Financial Action Task Force grey list.

[Compliance by legacy companies and digitisation of the corporate registry's records remain outstanding](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025). Business registration itself reaches the base only through the centralised service gateway that offers it as one of several services.

summary: A [diaspora health-workforce registry](2026-07-25-fg-commends-diaspora-health-professionals-nidah-portal) was launched standing on no stated legal basis.
developments:
It is described as newly launched, with no launch date, custodian agency, enrolment terms or data-protection basis stated in anything held: a register standing up ahead of its governance ([registry](2026-07-25-fg-commends-diaspora-health-professionals-nidah-portal)).

It is the pattern this unit repeats across the mortgage registry, the cooperative credential and the addressing framework, each announced before the instrument that would govern it.

summary: The [national social register expanded to 19.7m households](2025-06-12-nimc-id-prisoners-social-register-ai) from 13m, using artificial intelligence, satellite imagery and telecoms data to find urban-slum households.
developments:
The expansion used artificial intelligence, satellite imagery and telecoms data to reach households the register had missed, and 74 per cent of prison inmates hold an identity number ([register](2025-06-12-nimc-id-prisoners-social-register-ai)).

No exclusion, appeal or error measure for the register is published, and finding households by satellite and call-detail inference is a targeting method the data-protection regime does not separately address.

summary: [Biometric voter accreditation devices failed](2026-08-16-nba-election-working-group-osun-governorship-election-preliminary-report) at a state governorship election, with two observer missions calling for a technical audit before the 2027 general election.
developments:
The bar association's election working group recorded devices failing to boot and delaying a poll's opening, fingerprint and facial capture failing on some voters — elderly voters recurrently — so that they could not vote at all, slow processing at units of over 1,100 registered voters, an export failure and a complete device stoppage at one unit ([report](2026-08-16-nba-election-working-group-osun-governorship-election-preliminary-report)).

It recommends comprehensive pre-election testing of biometric capture, network connectivity, battery performance and volume handling, and an upgrade before the general election ([upgrade](2026-08-18-dailytrust-nba-osun-bvas-upgrade)); a second observer mission separately called for a full post-election technical audit ([audit](2026-08-16-nigeria-osun-yiaga-africa-bvas-audit)).

No commission response, failure rate or audit commitment is on record, and the observations are limited to the units the teams visited.

summary: A [Nigeria Digital Health Architecture](2025-12-19-state-nga-afghs-data-systems-2025-record) is named as the integration target of a United States health memorandum carrying US$196m for health data systems.
developments:
Health information, health services and health insurance claims exchanges are named as the integration target ([architecture](2025-12-19-state-nga-afghs-data-systems-2025-record), [memorandum](2025-12-19-afghs-mou-nigeria)).

US$196,000,000 of United States funding is planned for health data systems over 2026 to 2030 ([funding](2025-12-19-state-nga-afghs-data-systems-2025-record)). The architecture is named in a foreign instrument the government signed, and no Nigerian document setting it out is held.

summary: [Electronic cargo tracking](2026-07-29-thisday-ncs-electronic-cargo-tracking-system-ptml) replaced physical escort at a second command, while the [National Single Window](2026-08-07-nigeria-national-single-window-customs-dispute) is contested in operation by licensed customs agents.
developments:
Satellite tracking replaced physical escort of transit cargo at a second pilot command ([tracking](2026-07-29-thisday-ncs-electronic-cargo-tracking-system-ptml)).

The single window launched in March 2026 and is contested in operation: licensed customs agents say clearance paperwork has multiplied rather than consolidated, their association calling for the customs service to take over implementation outright and objecting to electronic manifest transmission outside the customs system. No throughput, clearance-time or adoption figure is published ([window](2026-08-07-nigeria-national-single-window-customs-dispute)).

summary: [Electronic filing became compulsory at the Supreme Court](2026-08-04-nigeria-digital-supreme-court-judicial-reform) from July 2026, behind a national case management system, with no judicial technology strategy to stop courts adopting incompatible systems.
developments:
Practice directions make electronic upload of processes and records of appeal compulsory, searchable and on standardised naming, inside a wider registry programme covering online senior-advocate applications, digital enrolment of practitioners, electronic registration of notaries and an electronic diary ([directions](2026-08-04-nigeria-digital-supreme-court-judicial-reform)).

A former state attorney-general argues the value is operations management rather than digitisation and calls for a national judicial technology strategy under the judicial council to stop each court adopting incompatible systems; no such strategy is held.

summary: A [single sign-on gateway](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services) is in pilot, a [centralised service gateway](2026-08-18-nigeria-centralised-gateway-portal-services-gov-ng) launched in August 2026, and neither states its relationship to the other.
developments:
The sign-on gateway is piloting on a four-year foreign-funded project reported at US$13m inside an electronic-government master plan ([gateway](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services)); the load-bearing feature is the once-only data exchange behind the login rather than the portal itself ([gateway](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services), [platform](2026-07-28-nigeria-unveils-unified-government-service-platform)).

A centralised gateway launched in August 2026 as a single point of access to federal services previously spread across agency websites, stated as a defence against fraudulent look-alike sites; no service count, transaction volume, cost or build attribution is published, and no relationship is stated to the sign-on gateway that soft-launched a month earlier ([services](2026-08-18-nigeria-centralised-gateway-portal-services-gov-ng)).

A central bank document-flow and payment solution has been live since January 2025 ([documents](2025-01-16-cbn-mda-naira-payment-docflow)), and the technology agency agreed to digitise pilgrimage operations end to end with no scope document, budget or timetable published ([pilgrimage](2026-08-19-nitda-nahcon-digitise-hajj-operations)).

A third platform was approved in the same period and sits outside both gateways: a smart national transport data bank, approved by the Federal Executive Council on a design-build-finance-operate-and-transfer model, to hold a nationwide central database of drivers, vehicles, number plates and operators and to standardise motor-park manifests ([approval](2026-08-31-thisdaylive-fg-unveils-major-rail-data-terminal-projects)). No cost, concession term or data-custody arrangement is disclosed for it.

summary: A [state services platform](2026-08-16-nigeria-anambra-onegov-digital-sme-formalisation) entered a second phase, a [state artificial-intelligence programme](2026-08-14-anambra-2030-ai-push-connectivity-test) is constrained by connectivity, and a [foreign-funded state reform project](2026-08-16-nigeria-ekiti-uk-digital-transformation-partnership) launched.
developments:
The state platform is expanding to digitise services and formalise small enterprises, logging about 14,000 visits over three weeks in July despite limited publicity ([platform](2026-08-16-nigeria-anambra-onegov-digital-sme-formalisation)); visits are not registrations or transactions and no service count, formalisation figure or cost is stated ([platform](2026-08-16-nigeria-anambra-onegov-digital-sme-formalisation), [partnership](2026-08-17-nigeria-undp-anambra-digital-economy-partnership)).

A state push on artificial intelligence and paperless government is constrained by weak connectivity and computing capacity on its own agency's account, with no budget, procurement, delivery date or named system published ([programme](2026-08-14-anambra-2030-ai-push-connectivity-test), [plan](2026-08-14-inside-anambra-s-2-0-plan-how-soludo-s-ict-agency-wants-ai-not-just-wi-fi-to-run)).

A foreign development project will produce a digital-economy strategy, an infrastructure roadmap, a civic-technology strategy and a connectivity-reform framework for one state, with value and duration not stated ([project](2026-08-16-nigeria-ekiti-uk-digital-transformation-partnership)); another state activated a multi-gigabit airport backbone ([airport](2026-08-18-akwa-ibom-victor-attah-airport-internet-backbone)).

summary: A [state artificial-intelligence platform](2025-06-30-anambra-ai-smartgov-lg-spending) flagged ₦2.1bn unspent and detected ghost workers, an [open-contracting platform](2025-02-06-ai-procurement-platform-states) runs in three states, and a [state trade programme](2026-07-31-enugu-tradex-afreximbank-smes) opened to 1,000 firms.
developments:
The state platform flagged a ₦2.1bn unspent education allocation and detected ghost workers through identity and bank-number cross-checks; the technology agency says under 10 per cent of government operations nationwide are digitised ([platform](2025-06-30-anambra-ai-smartgov-lg-spending)).

An artificial-intelligence open-contracting platform has run in three states since February 2025 ([contracting](2025-02-06-ai-procurement-platform-states)).

A state programme offers free digital storefronts, registration support, digital-trade training and payment enablement to 1,000 small firms, with cost, funder and selection method unstated ([trade](2026-07-31-enugu-tradex-afreximbank-smes)).

summary: A state's [260 smart green schools](2026-05-17-thecable-enugu-smart-schools-investigation-part-ii) at about ₦1.3-1.5bn each were promised open by January 2026 and many were incomplete, with roofs failed at three sites.
developments:
The programme covers 260 schools, one in each ward, powered by solar and connected by satellite, at about ₦1.3-1.5bn per school from state allocations of ₦266.7bn in 2025 and ₦198bn in 2026 ([investigation](2026-05-17-thecable-enugu-smart-schools-investigation-part-ii)).

Full opening of all 260 was promised for January 2026; as of May many were incomplete and unequipped with pupils already resuming, roofs had failed at three sites, one school was demolished after failing integrity tests, and a ₦11.4bn contract for 22 schools was terminated with ₦1.23bn recovered.

progress: Mixed, 3,700 towers contracted for unserved communities while only 23 per cent of rural communities have internet and zero-rating would require registration to use
summary: [23 per cent of rural communities have internet](2025-10-22-ncc-23pct-rural-internet-access) against 57 urban, [zero-rated education access](2026-06-19-ncc-consultation-paper-zero-rated-education-access) would require registration, and [rural job centres](2026-08-04-nigeria-skye-ii-giz-bmz-rural-job-centres-tender) are at equipment tender.
developments:
Rural internet reaches 23 per cent of communities against 57 per cent urban ([rural](2025-10-22-ncc-23pct-rural-internet-access)); the universal service fund plans 1,000 new rural base stations by 2030 and the minister told the President that about 3,700 towers start deploying around October 2026 targeting more than 20m people in communities with no service at all, with capital raised and no funding source, operator or contract named ([rural](2025-10-22-ncc-23pct-rural-internet-access), [stations](2025-03-20-1000-rural-base-stations), [towers](2026-08-04-nigeria-90000km-fibre-optic-rollout-tijani)).

Every eligibility option consulted on for zero-rated education access requires registration to control access and prevent abuse, the monitoring set includes tunnelling and streaming of non-educational content, and the regulator says on the record the scheme may breach net neutrality ([zero rating](2026-06-19-ncc-consultation-paper-zero-rated-education-access)).

Equipment for rural job centres in two states is out to tender under a foreign-funded youth-employment project, fixing the equipment stage and nothing about the centres ([centres](2026-08-04-nigeria-skye-ii-giz-bmz-rural-job-centres-tender)); agent-network microfinance reaches microenterprises through trained local agents with no published coverage figures ([microfinance](2026-07-20-rukayat-kolawole-bello-regxta)).

progress: Mixed, a disability-specific programme opened while the accessibility standard stalled and no audited public website met a baseline
summary: A [four-and-a-half-year programme](2026-08-18-lasoda-digital-futures-inclusion-workshop-lagos) for young people with disabilities opened in Lagos, while [none of eight public websites audited in May 2026 met baseline accessibility](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility).
developments:
The programme is run by a disability-rights organisation with a philanthropic foundation to expand employment access through digital skills, entrepreneurship and inclusive employment pathways, opened with the state disability office's stated support ([programme](2026-08-18-lasoda-digital-futures-inclusion-workshop-lagos)).

No budget, participant target or state-government commitment beyond stated support is published. It is the only disability-specific digital programme in the base for the country.

2026-08-31 — [none of eight public websites audited in May 2026, among them the admissions board, the identity commission, the revenue service and the disability commission itself, had baseline accessibility features](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility). [An earlier assessment of all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory found 26 non-compliant with the agency's website guidelines and 14 sites unusable for people with disabilities](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility) — different samples, not a series.

[The guidelines are in force and the web design standards meant to make them buildable published no toolkit a year on, while the regulator ran a fourth assistive-technology hackathon in Abuja on 26 and 27 August 2026](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility) — the assistive half of the problem, not the accessibility half. [An estimated 35 million Nigerians are persons with disabilities](2026-08-31-techcabal-assistive-tech-accessibility).

summary: A [digital self-care platform](2026-08-10-gomed-unfpa-digital-self-care-platform-university-of-lagos) went live for university students, routing to free contraceptives through the state health supply chain with discreet delivery.
developments:
The platform is live for students at one university and routes to free contraceptives via the state health ministry and an agency supply chain, with discreet delivery and pharmacist support, and expansion to other campuses planned ([platform](2026-08-10-gomed-unfpa-digital-self-care-platform-university-of-lagos)).

No user count, uptake figure or data-protection arrangement for reproductive-health requests is published, which is the sensitive-category question the country's own Act would reach.

summary: A [generative assistant](2025-02-03-ai-tool-public-service-efficiency) runs across the federal civil service, a [public-services chatbot](2026-05-22 Nigeria launches GovGuide, an AI chatbot for public service access) answers in four languages, and a state [automated its own agency operations](2026-08-17-nation-anambra-local-ai-government-automation) on an open model.
developments:
The civil-service assistant has been in service since February 2025 ([assistant](2025-02-03-ai-tool-public-service-efficiency)).

The public-services chatbot runs on an open foundation model in English and three Nigerian languages, pitched at rural, low-literacy and multilingual users, though poor rural broadband limits reach ([chatbot](2026-05-22 Nigeria launches GovGuide, an AI chatbot for public service access)).

A state technology agency reports modifying and training an open-source model to automate its own operations end to end and says it is exploring replication across state government; the account is the agency's own and no model, evaluation or measured saving is published ([automation](2026-08-17-nation-anambra-local-ai-government-automation)). A state survivor-support chatbot has been live since February 2025 ([survivor support](2025-02-25-ai-chatbot-domestic-violence-portal)).

summary: [Fraud detection was made mandatory](2026-06-09-cbn-ai-fraud-detection-realtime) in June 2026, [87.5 per cent of surveyed fintechs already use it](2026-02-01-cbn-policy-insight-series-2025-shaping-the-future-of-fintech-in-nigeria), and one firm [scores the unbanked from payment traces](2026-07-17-mathesis-analytics-raises-funding-ai-lending) and sells the output to lenders.
developments:
Artificial-intelligence and machine-learning fraud detection was made mandatory in June 2026 ([mandate](2026-06-09-cbn-ai-fraud-detection-realtime)).

A responsible artificial-intelligence in finance hub is proposed over an installed base: 87.5 per cent of the fintechs the central bank surveyed already use the technology for fraud detection, so production use is at near-saturation in a licensed sector under no national instrument and no model-risk rule ([hub](2026-02-01-cbn-policy-insight-series-2025-shaping-the-future-of-fintech-in-nigeria)).

One firm builds credit scores for people without bank accounts by reading payment traces, and sells the output to lenders; there is no published model-risk rule, no accuracy or adverse-impact measure and no route for a person to contest a score built this way ([scoring](2026-07-17-mathesis-analytics-raises-funding-ai-lending)).

summary: A [sovereign multilingual model](2025-09-22-n-atlas-nigerian-llm-launch) covers four Nigerian languages, a [code-switching speech model](2026-08-26-intron-sahara-v2-5-code-switching-voice-model) follows speakers who change language mid-sentence, and an [analysis agent](2026-07-17-decide-cafeone-enterprise-ai) is distributed through universities.
developments:
The sovereign model is open-source and multimodal across three Nigerian languages and Nigerian-accented English, built on an open foundation model and fine-tuned on more than 400m tokens; the country has more than 500 native languages ([model](2025-09-22-n-atlas-nigerian-llm-launch)).

A domestically built speech model was released to follow African speakers who switch languages mid-sentence, where most recognition systems transcribe the English and drop the other language; no accuracy benchmark against a named baseline, language list or deployment figure is published ([speech](2026-08-26-intron-sahara-v2-5-code-switching-voice-model)).

A spreadsheet-analysis agent is distributed through universities, co-working spaces and professional communities, its first partner bundling premium credits into member subscriptions; the governance point is that the co-working operator becomes the party mediating which tools its members meet and on what data terms ([agent](2026-07-17-decide-cafeone-enterprise-ai)).

summary: An [above US$470m surveillance estate](2026-03-24-nigeria-470m-ai-surveillance-spend) is the continent's largest with little evidence it reduces crime, and a [state facial-recognition network](2026-07-31-cross-river-smart-surveillance-infrastructure) was approved with no lawful basis stated.
developments:
A research mapping puts spend on facial recognition and number-plate tracking above US$470m with about 10,000 smart cameras, and researchers found little evidence it reduces crime and minimal use of footage in prosecutions ([estate](2026-03-24-nigeria-470m-ai-surveillance-spend)).

A state approved a first phase specified after engagements with a Chinese vendor, carrying facial recognition, plate recognition and violence detection across intersections, government precincts, coastal communities and a highway, feeding a command centre in the state security adviser's office; the claimed gains are emergency response falling from over 45 minutes to under 12, and no lawful basis, retention rule or oversight arrangement for the face and plate data is stated anywhere in the announcement ([network](2026-07-31-cross-river-smart-surveillance-infrastructure)).

A maritime surveillance system built for the navy is being pitched inland for banditry, with neither funding nor a political decision behind it, and its claimed returns are the vendor's own ([maritime](2026-08-05-falcon-eye-helped-nigeria-tackle-piracy-its-next-target-is-banditry)). A concessioned transport databank would put at least 250 gantries carrying plate recognition on the roads with traffic centres in every state ([databank](2026-08-20-von-nigeria-smart-transport-databank-committee)).

summary: Telecommunications reached [9.19 per cent of GDP](2026-07-30-thisday-telecoms-contribution-gdp-q1-2026), the [country-code domain passed 300,000 registrations](2026-01-21 How foreign domains compromise digital identity), and the [tower estate was consolidated](2026-08-26-ncc-mtn-ihs-conditional-approval-techcabal) under a single owner.
developments:
Telecommunications and information services reached 9.19 per cent of real GDP in the first quarter of 2026, a post-rebasing high, within information and communication at 11.31 per cent ([share](2026-07-30-thisday-telecoms-contribution-gdp-q1-2026)); a chamber of commerce figure of 10.07 per cent matches no official series, and the minister's tracking-close-to-21-per-cent claim is roughly double the official share and supported by no series the base holds, so it is recorded as a ministerial claim ([share](2026-07-30-thisday-telecoms-contribution-gdp-q1-2026)).

The country-code domain passed 300,000 registrations in 2025 ([domain](2026-01-21 How foreign domains compromise digital identity)), and 13,500 towers moved to a single infrastructure owner in a 2025 consolidation ([towers](2026-08-26-ncc-mtn-ihs-conditional-approval-techcabal)).

An operator has run domestic spam detection since March 2025 ([spam](2025-03-14-airtel-ai-spam-alert)), and a publication calculates about US$41m due to the state from a US$406m operator dividend, with no government confirmation of receipt held ([dividend](2026-08-19-nigeria-to-earn-41-million-from-mtns-406-million-dividend-payout)).

summary: The regulator [leased two federal facilities to a state](2026-08-04-ncc-digital-industrial-park-enugu-lease) after failing to activate them, a [digital free zone](2025-06-10-itana-first-digital-free-zone) runs remote incorporation, and [ten state hubs](2025-10-07-katsina-10bn-tech-hub-worldbank-bridge) are planned.
developments:
The regulator built buildings for outsourcing, incubation and skills and could not activate them, its executive vice chairman saying buildings alone do not create innovation, and leased them to the state for fifteen years to run as a talent city and an artificial-intelligence institute; both parties call the transfer temporary and reversible, and no rent, investment commitment or performance condition is stated ([lease](2026-08-04-ncc-digital-industrial-park-enugu-lease)).

The digital free zone is live for remote incorporation on a US$100m first-phase commitment from a continental financier ([zone](2025-06-10-itana-first-digital-free-zone)).

Ten state hubs are planned alongside the national talent programme ([hubs](2025-10-07-katsina-10bn-tech-hub-worldbank-bridge)), and a defence-technology firm holding a joint venture with the state arms corporation is to build robotics, drone and virtual-reality laboratories at a private university, with lab count, cost, funding, intake, research ownership and dual-use vetting all unstated ([laboratories](2026-08-03-itweb-nigeria-deep-tech-skills-miva-terra)).

summary: A [drive-to-own vehicle financier reached a US$2.1bn valuation](2026-08-07-moove-hits-21bn-unicorn-status) on a 42,000-vehicle fleet, a [diaspora remittance product was wound down](2026-08-25-moniepoint-monieworld-wind-down-techcabal), and the [largest payments processor folded in a third acquired brand](2026-08-31-paystack-acquires-allawee-nigeria-fintech).
developments:
About 25,000 small and medium enterprises are to receive N20bn in software credits under a vendor partnership with the small-business development agency ([announcement](2026-08-26-zoho-smedan-msme-tech-credits)). The credits are vendor-funded and the base holds no take-up figure.

The financier was founded in Nigeria in 2020 and is now headquartered in Dubai, raising US$250m at a US$2.1bn valuation against a 42,000-vehicle fleet across fourteen countries ([valuation](2026-08-07-moove-hits-21bn-unicorn-status)); the drive-to-own model makes ride-hailing platform earnings the credit-scoring and repayment rail for drivers outside formal banking, and no Nigerian instrument addresses that class of alternative-data underwriting ([valuation](2026-08-07-moove-hits-21bn-unicorn-status), [round](2026-08-05-techcrunch-moove-raises-250m-backbone-robotaxi-industry), [series](2026-08-06-connectingafrica-moove-250m-series-c)).

A Nigerian group is phasing out its United Kingdom diaspora remittance product less than eighteen months after launch, redirecting resources to Nigeria and Kenya, having committed 1.2 million pounds in setup expenditure and placed a US$2.5m equity deposit in July 2025 against US$7.39m earmarked in filings ([wind-down](2026-08-25-moniepoint-monieworld-wind-down-techcabal)).

A crowdsourced food-price platform reached about 2,500 users and extended into direct farmer-to-consumer sales ([prices](2026-08-10-nigeria-bango-price-data-food-markets)).

2026-08-31 — the largest payments processor is [winding down a card-issuing fintech acquired in an unannounced 2025 deal, closing its accounts on 1 December with balances and transaction history not carrying over](2026-08-31-paystack-acquires-allawee-nigeria-fintech) — the third brand folded in after a microfinance bank bought for its licence and a business-banking startup. No deal value is disclosed for any of them.

summary: One state trained [40,000 civil servants](2025-03-26-benue-40000-civil-servants-training), and a [data-protection officer pipeline](2025-05-06-mastercard-ndpc-informal-sector-dpo) targets 250,000 certifications a year in a sector that is 65 per cent of employment.
developments:
Forty thousand state civil servants were trained by March 2025 ([state training](2025-03-26-benue-40000-civil-servants-training)).

The officer pipeline targets 250,000 certified officers a year aimed at the informal sector, which is 65 per cent of employment and 58 per cent of gross domestic product, and the data-protection industry created 23,000 jobs in 2024 ([pipeline](2025-05-06-mastercard-ndpc-informal-sector-dpo), [academy](2025-05-07-nigeria-virtual-privacy-academy)).

The federal circular now requires every agency to appoint qualified officers, so the pipeline and the obligation arrived in the same period; no count of officers actually appointed across the federal service is published.

summary: A [technical education digital strategy](2026-08-12-nigeria-unesco-nbte-tvet-digital-transformation-strategy) was validated, [about 11,700 teachers](2026-07-31-nigeria-ai-training-unity-schools-teachers) are contracted for artificial-intelligence training, and [seventy teachers from 40 schools](2026-07-18-ness-2026-nigeria-education-summit) took a state programme.
developments:
The technical and vocational strategy was validated in August 2026 ([strategy](2026-08-12-nigeria-unesco-nbte-tvet-digital-transformation-strategy)).

A teacher capacity programme was contracted for national rollout to about 11,700 teachers across all federal unity colleges on the strength of a pilot in six colleges whose claimed results rest on the implementer's own account with no published evaluation ([teachers](2026-07-31-nigeria-ai-training-unity-schools-teachers)); neither the contract value, the funding source, the training duration nor the selection route for the contractor is stated ([teachers](2026-07-31-nigeria-ai-training-unity-schools-teachers)).

A state programme took seventy teachers drawn from 40 public schools, entering the classroom through teachers rather than the curriculum ([state](2026-07-18-ness-2026-nigeria-education-summit)).

2026-08-31 — the technology development agency [closed the 2026 edition of a school-holiday coding bootcamp in Kano, Kwara, Jigawa and Gombe, teaching coding, computational thinking and digital creativity, and states the same training continues in three southern zones](2026-08-31-techafricanews-nitda-trains-children-coding). No participant count, cost, partner list or curriculum is published, and the base holds no earlier edition against which to read it.

summary: [US$1.1m funds a train-the-trainer curriculum](2026-08-11-google-1-1m-ai-upskilling-nigeria-universities) at ten universities, a [national diploma in artificial intelligence](2026-08-10-nitda-nbte-ai-curriculum) launched for polytechnics, and a [university cybersecurity centre](2025-05-28-nitda-cybersecurity-centre-kano-buk) is operating.
developments:
The upskilling grant funds a train-the-trainer curriculum at ten Nigerian universities with a continental mathematical sciences institute; the country is the first of four, and the programme states 30 institutions across four countries and a target of more than 30,000 students, neither separately dated nor funded in the record ([grant](2026-08-11-google-1-1m-ai-upskilling-nigeria-universities), [programme](2026-08-11-google-nga-2026-aaup)).

A national diploma curriculum in artificial intelligence launched for polytechnics, and the board reports the technology has cut its own curriculum-development costs by about 50 per cent by generating draft curricula and courseware ([diploma](2026-08-10-nitda-nbte-ai-curriculum)).

A university cybersecurity centre has operated since May 2025 ([centre](2025-05-28-nitda-cybersecurity-centre-kano-buk)), and a training-of-trainers cohort was followed by a startup academy after 3,856 applications, with no cohort size, cost or completion figure published for either ([trainers](2026-08-21-koica-smedan-ace-startup-academy-2026-nigeria)).

summary: The [three-million talent programme](2026-08-04-nigeria-now-west-africas-digital-powerhouse-says-tijani) reports 1.87m registrations and more than 135,000 trained across three cohorts, a figure unmoved since January 2026.
developments:
Registrations run at 1.87m across all 774 local government areas with more than 135,000 trained across three cohorts and 15,000 job pathways created, against a target of information technology reaching 22 per cent of gross domestic product by 2027 ([programme](2026-08-04-nigeria-now-west-africas-digital-powerhouse-says-tijani)); the figures are the organisers' own and no independent evaluation is held ([programme](2026-08-04-nigeria-now-west-africas-digital-powerhouse-says-tijani), [commitment](2026-08-05-nitda-reaffirms-ai-commitment-launches-msme-training)).

The trained count is unmoved since at least January 2026, which is a stale-boilerplate flag rather than evidence of a higher count, and the programme has never stated whether it counts completion or enrolment. A ministerial figure of nearly 300,000 is the programme's own separate community-reach category, not a rival trained count ([placement](2026-05-06-3mtt-partners-hello-cv-to-place-nigerian-tech-talent-on-the-global-map)).

A free state academy targets 10,000 young people and 100 certified trainers ([academy](2026-08-10-lsetf-innopower-ekoai-academy-lagos)), two foundation programmes opened 2026 applications with no cohort size or placement figure published ([applications](2026-08-26-mastercard-foundation-cchub-gateway-digital-skills-nigeria)), and a private student aid scheme of 50 million naira opened for a single round ([aid](2026-08-18-startup-abuja-student-fund)).

2026-08-24 — a foundation-funded digital-skills programme began delivery with its [first orientation at a Kano polytechnic, its delivery partner stating it runs across ten states with three northern locations](2026-08-28-mastercard-foundation-gateway-ict-training-kano-nigeria). No cohort size, completion rate or placement figure is published.

summary: An [education-technology fellowship](2026-08-04-cchub-mastercard-foundation-edtech-fellowship-cohort-4) has supported 72 companies since 2019, and its fourth cohort funds education and workforce data systems in their own right.
developments:
The eighteen-month accelerator offers each company up to US$100,000 in equity-free funding and structured technical assistance, with twelve startups in cohort four and 72 companies supported since 2019 ([fellowship](2026-08-04-cchub-mastercard-foundation-edtech-fellowship-cohort-4)); the intake is targeted rather than open, across learners with disabilities, displacement-affected and rural communities, girls and young women, and education and workforce data systems, the fourth category funding sectoral education data infrastructure in its own right. The reach figure of more than 700,000 new learners is the hub's own ([fellowship](2026-08-04-cchub-mastercard-foundation-edtech-fellowship-cohort-4)).

A vendor-run academy sits inside a government skills initiative with a startup pitch competition and a developer bootcamp, its prize partly denominated in the sponsor's own advertising credits and no cohort size, curriculum or cost published ([academy](2026-08-17-meta-fmcide-3mtt-rain-ai-academy-nigeria)); a talent-export platform partnership has run since April 2025 ([export](2025-04-03-nitda-doballi-tech-talent-mou)).

summary: A second consecutive year of [free student artificial-intelligence subscriptions](2026-08-20-google-free-ai-access-nigerian-students) runs alongside a [US$1m commitment to train a million people](2025-02-19-microsoft-pledges-1m-ai-training) that drew feasibility scepticism at US$1 a trainee.
developments:
From August 2026 students at accredited universities, polytechnics and colleges of education get twelve months of a paid artificial-intelligence tier free, worth ₦92,400, the second consecutive year of the offer and one of 27 sub-Saharan rollouts, inside a five-area alliance running since February 2025 that put ₦3bn into Nigeria across five partners ([students](2026-08-20-google-free-ai-access-nigerian-students), [alliance](2025-02-13-nigeria-google-ai-alliance), [training](2025-11-28-google-n3bn-ai-training-programme)).

A US$1m commitment to train a million people over two years works out at US$1 a trainee, a ratio that drew feasibility scepticism ([commitment](2025-02-19-microsoft-pledges-1m-ai-training)).

A federal facility leased to a state is to run as a talent city and artificial-intelligence institute, with no capacity, occupancy or programme figure published ([talent city](2026-08-18-ncc-enugu-digital-industrial-park-lease)).

summary: A [first biometric census](2025-03-08-nigerias-first-biometric-census) remains planned with a budget of about ₦980bn under review, and the last census was 2006.
developments:
A committee will review the roughly ₦980bn budget, and no date has been set ([census](2025-03-08-nigerias-first-biometric-census)). Twenty years without a census is the baseline against which every population-denominated figure in this report has to be read.

An inclusive-data initiative widened from three countries to five in July 2026, putting the national statistics office into the programme ([initiative](2026-07-01-gpsdd-midn-dakar-peer-exchange)).

summary: A [vendor is in exploratory talks](2026-07-31-cisco-ai-nigeria-farmers) on artificial intelligence for smallholder farmers, with no programme, funding, timeline or counterparty ministry named.
developments:
The talks were reported in July 2026 and nothing beyond them is on record ([talks](2026-07-31-cisco-ai-nigeria-farmers)).

The farmer database planned for subsidy targeting is keyed to the identity register rather than to earth-observation data, so the base holds no operational agricultural use of satellite data for this country.

summary: A [hyperscaler began billing in naira](2025-01-14-aws-accepts-naira-payments), a [carrier-neutral facility opened](2025-11-10-equinix-lg3-22m-lagos-data-centre), a [card network built a data centre](2025-03-24-visa-data-centre-1-billion), and a [trade agency funded cloud-adoption training](2026-08-26-ustda-zenith-bank-nigeria-cloud-digital-banking-grant) at a Nigerian bank.
developments:
Naira billing began in January 2026, removing the foreign-exchange step from cloud spending ([billing](2025-01-14-aws-accepts-naira-payments)); a carrier-neutral facility opened in Lagos in June 2025 ([facility](2025-11-10-equinix-lg3-22m-lagos-data-centre)) and a card network built its own data centre in November 2025 ([card centre](2025-03-24-visa-data-centre-1-billion)).

A United States trade and development agency training grant to a Nigerian commercial bank supports its adoption of an American hyperscale cloud platform, funding training for senior managers on cloud governance and financial management; the grant amount is not stated, and the award moves a bank's workloads toward the foreign public cloud the base separately measures dependence on ([grant](2026-08-26-ustda-zenith-bank-nigeria-cloud-digital-banking-grant)).

A US$2m grant supports the 90,000 km fibre build alongside a feasibility grant for backbone reaching 12m people ([fibre](2025-01-15-us-nigeria-2m-fibre-deal), [feasibility](2025-01-15-ustda-nigeria-enhance-internet-access)).

summary: A [vendor innovation centre](2025-05-09-huawei-innovation-centre-lagos) was framed by the minister as a catalyst for technology sovereignty, a [vendor academy](2026-07-31-huawei-ncce-partner-to-expand-ai-digital-education-in-nigeria) sits inside the teacher-training accreditor, and an [agentic AI cloud](2026-08-31-techafricanews-huawei-agentic-ai-cloud-nigeria) launched locally in August 2026.
developments:
The Lagos innovation centre opened in May 2025 and was framed by the minister as a catalyst for the country's technology sovereignty, an unusually sovereignty-coded reception for a Chinese vendor ([centre](2025-05-09-huawei-innovation-centre-lagos)).

The academy sits at the commission itself and runs continuous training for lecturers and students, with the college curriculum revised to add artificial intelligence and robotics, networking and cybersecurity, data science and software development; no term, value or deliverable is published, so a single vendor's certification track is being written into the qualification route for the teachers who will go on to teach it ([academy](2026-07-31-huawei-ncce-partner-to-expand-ai-digital-education-in-nigeria)).

2026-08-27 — the vendor [launched an agentic artificial-intelligence cloud on its local infrastructure at its own Lagos summit, offered with data residency, security, compliance and low-latency claims for finance, telecommunications, internet services, government and enterprise](2026-08-31-techafricanews-huawei-agentic-ai-cloud-nigeria). [The technology development agency framed it against the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative and its ambition to move the country from consuming technology to hosting it](2026-08-31-techafricanews-huawei-agentic-ai-cloud-nigeria) — sovereignty language again attached to a foreign vendor's platform. No customer, contract, capacity or price is stated, and the residency claims are the vendor's own.

summary: A [EUR 820m digital envelope](2026-08-20-thisday-eu-820m-nigeria-innovation-hub-standard-framework) was stated at a workshop, a [EUR 45m package](2025-12-12-eu-45m-nigeria-digital-package) was signed in 2025, and a [Danish case-management platform](2026-01-15-cbrain-denmark-f2-egovernment) is deployed across federal ministries.
developments:
The envelope was stated at a framework validation workshop rather than in an instrument, alongside a national innovation hub standards framework that is validated rather than adopted ([envelope](2026-08-20-thisday-eu-820m-nigeria-innovation-hub-standard-framework), [gateway](2026-08-23-springer-teevan-evolution-digital-global-gateway)).

A digital economy package of EUR 45m was signed in December 2025 ([package](2025-12-12-eu-45m-nigeria-digital-package)).

The case-management platform is deployed with a Nigerian provider across federal ministries on the assurance that all sovereign data remains in Nigeria ([platform](2026-01-15-cbrain-denmark-f2-egovernment)). A cyber and digitalisation memorandum was signed with Finland in March 2026 ([cyber](2026-03-25-finland-nigeria-cyber-digitalisation-mou)), and Sweden signed a connectivity memorandum ([connectivity](2025-02-10-nigeria-sweden-connectivity-agreement)).

summary: A [2018 open data policy](2018-07-01-nigeria-open-data-policy) is still the operative framework, while the [open contracting portal](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025) is the one national dataset assessed as in use.
developments:
The [open data policy issued in July 2018](2018-07-01-nigeria-open-data-policy) remains the only national instrument expressly titled one, and no revision, review or compliance report under it is held.

The [public portal of the national education management platform](2026-06-29-dnemis-fg-unveils-national-digital-education-platform) is the first opening of a national administrative dataset to the public that the base records; no dataset list, licence or update cadence is published.

The [open contracting portal publishes standardised procurement data with custom dashboards for civil society and suppliers, and the procurement bureau reports about N173bn of savings in the first half of 2025](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025) - the only case in the base where published data is assessed against an outcome.

summary: The meteorological agency [completed installation of a Meteosat Third Generation receiving station](2025-05-09-nimet-mtg-satellite-installation) in May 2025 and nothing in the window touched the position.
developments: The [receiving station is the operative system through which the agency takes satellite data](2025-05-09-nimet-mtg-satellite-installation), installed before the window opened. No data volume, product list or downstream user figure is published, so what the station delivers into forecasting or early warning is unestablished.

summary: The [third national statistical strategy, covering 2024 to 2028](2025-12-14-nsds-iii-2024-2028-catalogue), is the operative instrument and nothing in the window moved it.
developments: The strategy is held as the [statistics bureau's own catalogue record](2025-12-14-nsds-iii-2024-2028-catalogue) rather than as the strategy text, which the base does not hold in readable form. No implementation report, funding line or mid-term review is published against it.

summary: The [Statistics Act 2007](2007-06-11-statistics-act-2007) is the standing legal base for the national statistical system, and nothing in the window changed it.
developments: The [Act established the National Statistical System and the statistics bureau](2007-06-11-statistics-act-2007) and remains operative pending passage of the Statistics Bill 2025. The base holds no rule, framework or published series governing the use of administrative data as a statistical source.

summary: The primary health care agency [operates a data-aggregation hub for primary health centre data](2025-07-21-nphcda-digital-innovation-hub), and nothing dated in the window moved it.
developments: The [hub is the clearest primary statement the base holds of an existing instrument for digitising the primary health layer](2025-07-21-nphcda-digital-innovation-hub). It is an institutional description rather than a dated report: no facility count, coverage figure or data-quality statement is published, so how far it reaches rural clinics is unestablished.

summary: The interior ministry [describes biometric capture at divisional police stations nationwide](2024-12-02-national-data-fusion-centre-npcidb) feeding a national criminal information database; nothing in the window moved it.
developments: The [ministry's own account of the national criminal data fusion centre](2024-12-02-national-data-fusion-centre-npcidb) sets out capture at divisional stations built on the West African police information system and a regional criminal-records framework. No station count, capture volume or coverage figure is published, so how far the capture actually reaches rural divisions is unestablished.

progress: Mixed, the registry went fully digital while the health-facility notification layer did not start
summary: Civil registration [went nationwide on a digital platform with paper discontinued from 1 July 2026](2026-07-18-nigeria-crvs-digitalisation-vitalreg), while [none of 371 targeted health facilities went live](2026-08-22-vanguard-nigeria-birth-registration-gap).
developments:
The [country case on the registry platform](2026-07-18-nigeria-crvs-digitalisation-vitalreg) records ward-level coverage and the platform as the operative system for civil registration and vital statistics.

Against that, [paper registration was discontinued from 1 July 2026 but none of 371 targeted health facilities were live despite completed training, and zero birth notifications were flowing from them](2026-08-22-vanguard-nigeria-birth-registration-gap) — the layer that would reach births outside registry offices.

summary: A [national education data platform](2026-06-29-dnemis-fg-unveils-national-digital-education-platform) was announced in June 2026 to unify school, learner, teacher and infrastructure records, above a [learner identification number](2026-08-05-nigeria-integrates-national-student-ids-digital-identity-system) issued from April 2026.
developments:
The [platform is the flagship of the national education data infrastructure, unifying school, learner, teacher and infrastructure records into one national database with a public portal](2026-06-29-dnemis-fg-unveils-national-digital-education-platform); it is a pre-launch announcement, and no school, learner or record count and no go-live confirmation is held.

The [16-digit learner identification number was issued from April 2026, 1.9 million at launch, integrated with the national identification register through the education management information system](2026-08-05-nigeria-integrates-national-student-ids-digital-identity-system).

summary: The health ministry [puts 7.2 million people on the national health information exchange and more than 200 hospitals integrated](2025-11-20-nch-2025-salako-digital-health-remarks); nothing later moved it.
developments: The figures are the [minister of state for health's own, given in opening remarks to the National Council on Health in November 2025](2025-11-20-nch-2025-salako-digital-health-remarks), and are the strongest official evidence the base holds of the exchange's standing. No independent count, facility list or integration standard is published, and no later figure is held.

summary: The [national data exchange went into production behind the government service portal](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services), and its [draft technical standard names social-benefit payments among intended services](2025-03-17-nitda-dpi-technical-standards-draft-v1-3).
developments:
The [exchange is in production behind the government service portal](2026-07-30-nigeria-unveils-digital-govt-platform-for-unified-access-to-public-services), though the lawful basis on which it moves personal data is not on record.

Its [own draft technical standard, version 1.3 of 17 March 2025, specifies the exchange architecture and explicitly includes government subsidies and social-benefit payments as an intended service](2025-03-17-nitda-dpi-technical-standards-draft-v1-3); the standard is marked draft and the base holds no adopted version.

summary: A [new identity commission Act was assented in June 2026](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act), and the population commission states [under-fives receive an identity number at birth registration](2024-08-26-npc-unicef-first-lady-partner-birth-registration).
developments:
The [Act replaced the 2007 statute as the legal foundation of the national identity system](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act) and makes the national identification number the foundational credential.

The population commission [states that under-five children are to receive a national identification number at the point of birth registration and that its electronic civil registration system is interoperable with the identity commission](2024-08-26-npc-unicef-first-lady-partner-birth-registration); no figure for numbers issued at birth is published.

summary: The population commission states its [civil registration system is interoperable with the identity commission](2024-08-26-npc-unicef-first-lady-partner-birth-registration), and a [new identity Act](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act) strengthened the legal basis for that exchange.
developments:
The commission's [own dated statement puts the electronic civil registration system as interoperable with the identity commission and other identity agencies, with access to immunisation and social-welfare records](2024-08-26-npc-unicef-first-lady-partner-birth-registration).

The [identity commission Act 2026](2026-07-30-pros-cons-of-amended-nimc-act) replaced the 2007 statute and made the national identification number the foundational credential, strengthening the legal basis for registry-to-identity data exchange. No volume of records exchanged is published.

summary: A [16-digit learner identification number](2026-08-05-nigeria-integrates-national-student-ids-digital-identity-system) was issued from April 2026 on the education management information system, whose [founding policy dates from 2021](2021-08-01-reviewed-national-policy-on-emis).
developments:
The [policy approved by the National Council on Education and signed in August 2021 established the national, state and local education management information systems](2021-08-01-reviewed-national-policy-on-emis), reviewing the original 2007 and 2009 policy.

On that base, the [learner identification number was issued from April 2026, 1.9 million at launch, integrated with the national identification register](2026-08-05-nigeria-integrates-national-student-ids-digital-identity-system).

summary: The housing minister stated in March 2025 that [no unified national land information system existed and under 10 per cent of land is registered](2025-03-19-fmhud-keynote-national-land-registration-documentation-programme); nothing in the window moved it.
developments: The [minister's keynote to the national land registration and documentation programme workshop](2025-03-19-fmhud-keynote-national-land-registration-documentation-programme) set out the absence and a plan to develop and launch a national digital land information system with the World Bank. No build stage, budget, operator or launch date has since been published, so the position at the end of the window is the position at the start.

summary: The [social register stands at 19.7 million households](2025-06-12-nimc-id-prisoners-social-register-ai) and the [safety-net programme reports identity validation and fully digital payments](2025-09-03-worldbank-nassp-su-implementation-status-results-report) operating; nothing in the window moved either.
developments:
The [register grew from 13 million to 19.7 million households](2025-06-12-nimc-id-prisoners-social-register-ai) before the window opened.

The [World Bank's implementation status report of September 2025 records the delivery-system-strengthening component operating: the social register, validation against the national identification number, and fully digital payments to verified beneficiary-owned accounts](2025-09-03-worldbank-nassp-su-implementation-status-results-report). No later figure or outturn is held.

summary: The [central bank digital currency whose guidelines defined government-to-person transaction types](2021-10-25-cbn-regulatory-guidelines-on-the-enaira) is [being redesigned toward a wholesale model](2026-07-26-nigeria-payment-vision-2028), removing the retail channel.
developments:
The [2021 regulatory guidelines established the currency under the central bank Act and the banking Act and explicitly defined person-to-government and government-to-person transactions, and transactions from ministries, departments and agencies to persons](2021-10-25-cbn-regulatory-guidelines-on-the-enaira) — the primary legal basis the base holds for government-to-person payment capability on that rail.

The currency is now [being redesigned toward a wholesale model](2026-07-26-nigeria-payment-vision-2028), which withdraws the retail leg those provisions describe. No replacement retail government-to-person rail is named.

summary: The [Tax Administration Act 2025](2025-06-26-nigeria-tax-administration-act-2025) requires every taxable person and every government body to register and obtain a taxpayer identification; nothing in the window moved the register itself.
developments: The [Act, gazetted 26 June 2025, requires registration and a taxpayer identification for every taxable person and for federal, state and local government bodies, at sections 4 to 10](2025-06-26-nigeria-tax-administration-act-2025). The base holds no register size, coverage figure or registration outturn under it, so the register's own position is unestablished.

summary: No single umbrella instrument exists; the finance ministry's [international economic relations department](2026-08-28-international-economic-relations-department) is the administrative home of the relationships, and nothing in the window moved it.
developments: The [department manages bilateral and multilateral economic relationships, memoranda of understanding and concessional financing](2026-08-28-international-economic-relations-department). The page is undated on the ministry site and carries no list of relationships, agreements or financing volumes, so what the strategic relationships consist of is unestablished from it.

summary: A [comprehensive economic partnership agreement with the United Arab Emirates](2026-01-13-nigeria-uae-cepa) was signed on 13 January 2026, the most significant Gulf instrument the base holds.
developments: The [agreement was signed on 13 January 2026 and explained publicly by the trade minister](2026-01-13-nigeria-uae-cepa). The agreement text is not held, and no digital or data chapter is published, so what it carries for the digital economy is unestablished.

summary: The [joint statement of the 2024 state visit](2024-11-17-india-nigeria-joint-statement-modi-visit) records a computer emergency response team memorandum on cyber security; nothing in the window added to it.
developments: The [statement names cyber security, fintech and space among the fields of the Strategic Partnership, records a memorandum between the two national computer emergency response teams, and carries an Indian offer to share its open-source health-management digital infrastructure](2024-11-17-india-nigeria-joint-statement-modi-visit). The text of the memorandum the Nigerian minister signed with India's electronics and information technology ministry is still not held.

summary: The [Freedom of Information Act 2011](2011-05-28-freedom-of-information-act-2011) is the standing access-to-information statute and nothing in the window touched it.
developments: The [Act was passed on 24 May 2011 and assented to on 28 May 2011](2011-05-28-freedom-of-information-act-2011) and remains in force. The base holds no compliance report, request-volume figure or refusal statistic under it, so how the right is exercised in practice is unestablished.

summary: The [Statistics Act 2007](2007-06-11-statistics-act-2007-official-gazette) remains operative pending the Statistics Bill 2025, and nothing in the window moved it.
developments: The [Act, gazetted 11 June 2007, established the National Statistical System and the statistics bureau](2007-06-11-statistics-act-2007-official-gazette). The base holds no dated stage for the Statistics Bill 2025 that would replace it, so the standing position is the 2007 statute.

summary: The [2018 open data policy](2018-07-01-nigeria-open-data-policy) is the only national instrument expressly titled one and remains the operative framework; nothing in the window revised it.
developments: The [policy was issued in July 2018 by the communications ministry and still governs the national open-data portal and agency publication obligations](2018-07-01-nigeria-open-data-policy). No revision, review or compliance report under it is held, so whether agencies meet its obligations is unestablished.

summary: A [presidency citizens e-feedback portal](2025-03-15-servicom-e-citizens-feedback-portal) launched in March 2025 with an initial cohort of agencies onboarded; nothing in the window moved it.
developments: The [service-compliance office launched the portal in March 2025 on an open-government basis, with an initial group of ministries, departments and agencies onboarded](2025-03-15-servicom-e-citizens-feedback-portal). No complaint volume, resolution rate or agency-coverage figure has been published since, so the portal's use is unestablished.

summary: The 2023-2025 action plan closed with its [open-budget commitments named among those that did not achieve their intended results](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025).
developments:
The [commitment on citizen participation across the budget cycle](2023-01-01-ogp-nigeria-citizen-participation-budget-cycle) was carried in the 2023 action plan.

The independent reporting mechanism's final report on that plan, published 28 April 2026, [names the open-budget commitments among those that did not achieve their intended results](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025), attributing this partly to the leadership transitions that followed the 2023 elections.

Participation in the plan's own co-creation was [concentrated in Abuja and Lagos, with high logistics costs and accessibility barriers limiting it elsewhere](2026-04-28-ogp-nigeria-results-report-2023-2025). No successor budget-participation commitment is held.

summary: The [2022 Act founding the refugees, migrants and displaced persons commission](2022-12-28-ncfrmi-act-2022-full-text) is the standing legal basis, and its full text is now held.
developments:
The [Act is the founding statute for the national institution responsible for refugees, migrants and internally displaced persons](2022-12-28-ncfrmi-act-2022-full-text) and the operative legal basis for their inclusion in public services.

The full text puts a registry function in statute: the Commission is to [register and personally document persons of concern, and support state governments to create and maintain updated registers of them](2022-12-28-ncfrmi-act-2022-full-text).

No registration, identification or service-access figure under those functions is published, and no register is named as operating.

summary: The last official national statement is the [2020 broadband plan: six submarine cables at Lagos, over 40 Tbps available and under 10 per cent used](2020-03-01-nigerian-national-broadband-plan-2020-2025).
developments: The [plan, whose term ran to 2025, carries the last clear official statement of international capacity, dated January 2020](2020-03-01-nigerian-national-broadband-plan-2020-2025). No successor plan and no later official figure is held, so the position at the end of the window is a six-year-old statement — which is itself the finding.

summary: The regulator reports [frequency and voltage outside the Grid Code range, 7.96 per cent transmission loss and a total grid collapse on 23 January 2026](2026-07-01-nerc-q1-2026-quarterly-report).
developments:
The [regulator's statutory first-quarter 2026 report records frequency and voltage outside the Grid Code range, 7.96 per cent transmission loss, 32.72 per cent plant availability, a total grid collapse on 23 January 2026 and a partial collapse on 27 January](2026-07-01-nerc-q1-2026-quarterly-report).

The standing position it sits against is that the [grid has never reliably exceeded 6 GW for about 230 million people, roughly 41 per cent availability](2026-05-21 Africa Data Center Investment 2026 The $4.5B Race and the Power Problem).
